chunks.text: NEWS RELEASE: Sen. Ashley Moody Fights to Protect Florida’s Coast from Off-Shore Oil Drilling, Introduces the American Shores Protection Act   - Senator Moody NEWS RELEASE: Sen. Ashley Moody Fights to Protect Florida’s Coast from Off-Shore Oil Drilling, Introduces the American Shores Protection Act

chunks.title: NEWS RELEASE: Sen. Ashley Moody Fights to Protect Florida’s Coast from Off-Shore Oil Drilling, Introduces the American Shores Protection Act   - Senat
chunks.text: WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Senator Ashley Moody announced she is introducing the American Shores Protection Act to prohibit oil drilling and natural gas exploration and development near Florida’s coastline. This legislation would extend the drilling moratorium, which includes the shores of Florida, Georgia, and South Carolina, from 2022 to 2032, and would codify President Trump’s September 2020 executive action that protects Sunshine State beaches.

chunks.title: NEWS RELEASE: Sen. Ashley Moody Fights to Protect Florida’s Coast from Off-Shore Oil Drilling, Introduces the American Shores Protection Act   - Senat
chunks.text: Senator Ashley Moody said, “As a fifth-generation Floridian, preserving our state’s natural beauty is deeply important to me and the millions of those who call the Sunshine State home—as well as those who come to visit and vacation. It is my mission to protect our state’s coastline for the next generation. Florida has made significant efforts to conserve its incredible natural resources, and I will continue this fight at the federal level. I appreciate my colleagues’ support as we work together to ensure oil drilling stays off our beaches and pass the American Shores Protection Act.”

chunks.title: NEWS RELEASE: Sen. Ashley Moody Fights to Protect Florida’s Coast from Off-Shore Oil Drilling, Introduces the American Shores Protection Act   - Senat
chunks.text: This bill would codify the Eastern Gulf of Mexico Moratorium (EGOM) President Trump issued through 2032. The U.S. House in 2019 voted 248-180 on a resolution (HR 205) to make the drilling moratorium in the Gulf of Mexico permanent. Later that year, nearly 70% of Florida voters approved a constitutional amendment that reinforced a ban on drilling in state waters off the coastlines. Senators Rick Scott and Lindsey Graham have cosponsored the legislation.

chunks.title: NEWS RELEASE: Senators Ashley Moody & Rick Scott Lead Bipartisan Florida Delegation Letter to President Trump: Keep Oil Drilling Off Florida’s Coasts
chunks.text: NEWS RELEASE: Senators Ashley Moody & Rick Scott Lead Bipartisan Florida Delegation Letter to President Trump: Keep Oil Drilling Off Florida’s Coasts - Senator Moody NEWS RELEASE: Senators Ashley Moody & Rick Scott Lead Bipartisan Florida Delegation Letter to President Trump: Keep Oil Drilling Off Florida’s Coasts

chunks.title: NEWS RELEASE: Senators Ashley Moody & Rick Scott Lead Bipartisan Florida Delegation Letter to President Trump: Keep Oil Drilling Off Florida’s Coasts
chunks.text: WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Senator Ashley Moody and Senator Rick Scott led Florida’s entire congressional delegation in sending a letter to President Trump encouraging him to reject any potential plans from the Department of Interior that would violate his moratorium banning oil drilling off Florida’s coasts. The members note that Florida’s coasts are an iconic and pristine part of the state’s environment, serve as a critical national security point for military training with the Gulf Test Range, and help generate jobs and over $127 billion in annual tourism spending.

chunks.title: NEWS RELEASE: Senators Ashley Moody & Rick Scott Lead Bipartisan Florida Delegation Letter to President Trump: Keep Oil Drilling Off Florida’s Coasts
chunks.text: Additionally, in October, Senator Moody announced she is introducing the American Shores Protection Act to prohibit oil drilling and natural gas exploration and development near Florida’s coastline. This legislation would extend the drilling moratorium, which includes the shores of Florida, Georgia, and South Carolina, from 2022 to 2032, and would codify President Trump’s September 2020 executive action that protects Sunshine State beaches.

chunks.title: NEWS RELEASE: Senators Ashley Moody & Rick Scott Lead Bipartisan Florida Delegation Letter to President Trump: Keep Oil Drilling Off Florida’s Coasts
chunks.text: We write as members of Florida’s congressional delegation to express our strong opposition to any attempts to expand offshore oil and gas drilling off Florida’s coasts. In 2020, you made the right decision to use executive action to extend the moratorium on oil and gas leasing off Florida’s gulf and east coasts through 2032, recognizing the incredible value Florida’s pristine coasts have to our state’s economy, environment, and military community. This move received overwhelming and bipartisan support.

chunks.title: NEWS RELEASE: Senators Ashley Moody & Rick Scott Lead Bipartisan Florida Delegation Letter to President Trump: Keep Oil Drilling Off Florida’s Coasts
chunks.text: The recent announcement from the Department of the Interior’s Bureau of Ocean Energy Management (BOEM) on their proposed five-year offshore leasing plan, announced November 20, 2025, includes a “new” planning area called the South-Central Gulf of America. If this plan were to move forward, the area would clearly fall within the area protected under your moratorium in a clear violation of your 2020 Executive Order. This area also falls within the Gulf Test Range, a critical military training area used by several military forces along Florida’s Panhandle for advanced military testing, training, and evaluation of air and weapons systems.

chunks.title: NEWS RELEASE: Senators Ashley Moody & Rick Scott Lead Bipartisan Florida Delegation Letter to President Trump: Keep Oil Drilling Off Florida’s Coasts
chunks.text: The Gulf Test Range, remains an integral part of Department of War training to ensure mission readiness and is supported by multiple military bases in Florida’s Panhandle. Collectively, these bases employ tens of thousands of military and civilian personnel and are of critical importance to national security. Eglin Air Force Base alone supports 20,000 personnel, provides the country with $11 billion in economic impact every year, and currently boasts 123,000 square miles of water range, which would all have to be reduced in an instance of an encroachment of the Gulf Test Range.

chunks.title: NEWS RELEASE: Senators Ashley Moody & Rick Scott Lead Bipartisan Florida Delegation Letter to President Trump: Keep Oil Drilling Off Florida’s Coasts
chunks.text: The Gulf Test Range is the largest multi-domain military training and testing complex in the country, and its unique geographic characteristics enable critical preparation for real-world contingencies. Protecting this range from encroachment, including oil exploration, is essential. Over 50,000 jobs in the Panhandle depend directly on operations at these military facilities connected to the Gulf Test Range.

chunks.title: NEWS RELEASE: Senators Ashley Moody & Rick Scott Lead Bipartisan Florida Delegation Letter to President Trump: Keep Oil Drilling Off Florida’s Coasts
chunks.text: Florida’s economy relies on that same beautiful coastline, vibrant tourism industry, and sustainable fisheries. In fact, Florida’s beaches alone generate more than $127.7 billion per year in tourism spending and support over 2.1 million tourism-related jobs. Unfortunately, all these resources suffered devastating harm during the Deepwater Horizon oil spill of 2010. That disaster wiped billions of dollars from Florida’s industries and caused irreparable damage to our environment and coastal communities. The risks posed by new offshore drilling far outweigh any short-term gains.

chunks.title: NEWS RELEASE: Senators Ashley Moody & Rick Scott Lead Bipartisan Florida Delegation Letter to President Trump: Keep Oil Drilling Off Florida’s Coasts
chunks.text: For these reasons, we urge you to uphold your existing moratorium and keep Florida’s coasts off the table for oil and gas leasing. Florida’s economy, environment, and military readiness depend on this commitment. Thank you for your consideration and leadership in preserving Florida’s coast and security.

chunks.title: VIDEO RELEASE: Sen. Moody on the Senate Floor: I’ll Keep Fighting to Protect Florida’s Coast from Off-Shore Oil Drilling, Secures Commitment to Move A
chunks.text: WASHINGTON, D.C.— Today, Senator Ashley Moody took to the Senate Floor to request unanimous consent on her American Shores Protection Act – continuing her fight in keeping oil drilling off Florida’s coast. In October, Senator Moody announced the introduction of her American Shores Protection Act to prohibit oil drilling and natural gas exploration and development near Florida’s coastline. This legislation would extend Florida’s drilling moratorium from 2022 to 2032, and would codify President Trump’s September 2020 executive action that protects Sunshine State beaches. Senator Rick Scott, the bill’s cosponsor, joined Senator Moody in this request.

chunks.title: VIDEO RELEASE: Sen. Moody on the Senate Floor: I’ll Keep Fighting to Protect Florida’s Coast from Off-Shore Oil Drilling, Secures Commitment to Move A
chunks.text: While the legislation did not pass by unanimous consent today, Senator Mike Lee, the objector and Chairman of the Energy and Natural Resources Committee, gave his commitment to bring the legislation up in its committee of jurisdiction and move forward on the lawmaking process.

chunks.title: VIDEO RELEASE: Sen. Moody on the Senate Floor: I’ll Keep Fighting to Protect Florida’s Coast from Off-Shore Oil Drilling, Secures Commitment to Move A
chunks.text: “I rise today to move for unanimous consent on the American Shores Protection Act. This would codify President Trump’s 2020 moratorium on drilling off Florida’s Gulf of America and Atlantic Coasts. Florida has worked with President Trump for years to keep these operations off our pristine coasts…because our coasts are a vital component of our state’s economic success. In fact, Florida’s beaches alone generate more than $127.7 billion a year in tourism spending and support more than 2.1 million related jobs…”

chunks.title: VIDEO RELEASE: Sen. Moody on the Senate Floor: I’ll Keep Fighting to Protect Florida’s Coast from Off-Shore Oil Drilling, Secures Commitment to Move A
chunks.text: “However, these great resources are vulnerable to risks posed by new offshore drilling. We all saw the devastating harm caused by the Deepwater Horizon oil spill in 2010—that disaster wiped billions of dollars from Florida’s industries and caused horrific damage to our environment and coastal communities…” “Our coasts also play an important role in securing our nation. The Gulf Test Range, a big part of the Department of War’s training to ensure mission readiness, is supported by multiple military bases in Florida’s panhandle. More than 50,000 jobs in the Panhandle depend directly on operations at military facilities in this area…”

chunks.title: VIDEO RELEASE: Sen. Moody on the Senate Floor: I’ll Keep Fighting to Protect Florida’s Coast from Off-Shore Oil Drilling, Secures Commitment to Move A
chunks.text: “As a fifth-generation Floridian, preserving our state’s natural beauty is deeply important to me and…the millions of those who call the Sunshine State home—as well as those who come to visit and vacation. It is my mission to protect our state’s coastline—from Pensacola Beach where the Blue Angels fly to Duval Street in Key West. From the iconic South Beach, Miami to Fernandina in the very tip of Northeast Florida—all for our next generation…”

chunks.title: VIDEO RELEASE: Sen. Moody on the Senate Floor: I’ll Keep Fighting to Protect Florida’s Coast from Off-Shore Oil Drilling, Secures Commitment to Move A
chunks.text: The American Shores Protection Act would codify the Eastern Gulf of Mexico Moratorium (EGOM) President Trump issued through 2032. The U.S. House in 2019 voted 248-180 on a resolution (HR 205) to make the drilling moratorium in the Gulf of Mexico permanent. Later that year, nearly 70% of Florida voters approved a constitutional amendment that reinforced a ban on drilling in state waters off the coastlines. Senators Rick Scott and Lindsey Graham have cosponsored the legislation.

chunks.title: Senator Moody Fights to Protect Eglin Gulf Test and Training Range - Senator Moody
chunks.text: Senator Moody Fights to Protect Eglin Gulf Test and Training Range - Senator Moody Senator Moody Fights to Protect Eglin Gulf Test and Training Range WASHINGTON, D.C.— Senator Ashley Moody is fighting to protect an important national military asset in Northwest Florida. Senator Moody has joined Senator Rick Scott in championing the Protecting Florida’s Offshore Military Readiness Act to prohibit drilling oil and gas inside the Eglin Gulf Test and Training Range.

chunks.title: Senator Moody Fights to Protect Eglin Gulf Test and Training Range - Senator Moody
chunks.text: “The Eglin Gulf Test and Training Range is a national military asset that can’t be replicated anywhere else in the world, and the work done there directly shapes the lethality of our future military. I’m proud to join Senator Scott on the Protecting Florida’s Offshore Military Readiness Act to keep the range as exactly what it was intended to be—a testing ground. Protecting Eglin is about our national security, and it’s about preserving the Gulf Coast Floridians love,” said Senator Ashley Moody .

chunks.title: Senator Moody Fights to Protect Eglin Gulf Test and Training Range - Senator Moody
chunks.text: “The federal government’s first priority is to keep the American people safe. That means our military needs the irreplaceable value that the Eglin Gulf Test and Training Range provides to our warfighters. Protecting the range means protecting America’s military readiness. I am glad to have Sen. Moody’s support on this bill, and I look forward to working with President Trump and his administration to use every tool we have to deliver more abundant, cheap energy while ensuring our military remains the most lethal fighting force on Earth,” said Senator Rick Scott .

chunks.title: Senator Moody Fights to Protect Eglin Gulf Test and Training Range - Senator Moody
chunks.text: The legislation aims to protect the critical Eglin Gulf Test and Training Range from interference that could hamper the U.S. Department of War’s ability to maintain readiness in the Gulf of America. The EGTTR is a key national security asset that provides the U.S. military with vital air, sea, and joint testing and training capabilities. Senator Moody is a proud supporter of the U.S. Armed Forces, veterans, and military families. Senator Moody recently joined the  Senate Armed Services Committee . Last year, Senator Moody  recognized 200 years of U.S. Navy presence in Pensacola and discussed the critical importance of the Navy and Coast Guard’s presence in the Florida Panhandle .

chunks.title: Senator Moody Fights to Protect Eglin Gulf Test and Training Range - Senator Moody
chunks.text: Senator Moody has long fought for Florida’s military members. As Florida Attorney General, Moody oversaw the Military and Veterans Assistance Program to assist servicemembers, veterans and their families who encounter scams or fraud. Senator Moody is proud to be part of a military family.

chunks.title: Senator Ashley Moody and Senator Rick Scott Announce Legislation to Include Osceola Camp in Miccosukee Reserved Area - Senator Moody
chunks.text: Senator Ashley Moody and Senator Rick Scott Announce Legislation to Include Osceola Camp in Miccosukee Reserved Area - Senator Moody Senator Ashley Moody and Senator Rick Scott Announce Legislation to Include Osceola Camp in Miccosukee Reserved Area

chunks.title: Senator Ashley Moody and Senator Rick Scott Announce Legislation to Include Osceola Camp in Miccosukee Reserved Area - Senator Moody
chunks.text: WASHINGTON, D.C. — Florida’s U.S. Senators Ashley Moody and Rick Scott announced the Miccosukee Reserved Area Amendments Act designating the Osceola Camp in Everglades National Park as a part of the Miccosukee Reservation. The legislation will help optimize water flow into Everglades National Park while taking steps to protect the Osceola Camp against flooding risks. Congressman Carlos Gimenez is leading this legislation in the House of Representatives, and this legislation is supported by the Miccosukee Tribe.

chunks.title: Senator Ashley Moody and Senator Rick Scott Announce Legislation to Include Osceola Camp in Miccosukee Reserved Area - Senator Moody
chunks.text: Senator Ashley Moody said, “As a 5 th generation Floridian, protecting the state’s natural beauty is one of my top priorities. This legislation makes great strides in ensuring that the benefits of Everglades restoration can be achieved while also protecting Miccosukee Tribe members who call the Everglades home.”

chunks.title: Senator Ashley Moody and Senator Rick Scott Announce Legislation to Include Osceola Camp in Miccosukee Reserved Area - Senator Moody
chunks.text: Senator Rick Scott said, “ The Miccosukee Tribe’s Osceola Camp has been a home and site of cultural significance for generations of Tribal members and I am proud to introduce this bill with Senator Ashley Moody and our colleagues to ensure its protection. I deeply appreciate the partnership I have had with the Miccosukee Tribe as Florida’s Governor, and will continue to support their interests as U.S. Senator. ”

chunks.title: Senator Ashley Moody and Senator Rick Scott Announce Legislation to Include Osceola Camp in Miccosukee Reserved Area - Senator Moody
chunks.text: Congressman Carlos Gimenez said, “As the Representative for the Miccosukee Tribe, I have seen firsthand the Tribe’s dedication to being outstanding stewards of the Everglades, as well as their role as a vital community partner, fostering jobs and opportunities for South Floridians. I am eager to continue collaborating with the Tribe to protect our cherished River of Grass and integrate the Osceola Camp into the Miccosukee Reserved Area.”

chunks.title: VIDEO: Senator Moody Secures Nearly $2 Billion in FEMA Recovery Assistance for Florida Communities Hit by Major Hurricanes - Senator Moody
chunks.text: VIDEO: Senator Moody Secures Nearly $2 Billion in FEMA Recovery Assistance for Florida Communities Hit by Major Hurricanes - Senator Moody VIDEO: Senator Moody Secures Nearly $2 Billion in FEMA Recovery Assistance for Florida Communities Hit by Major Hurricanes PUNTA GORDA, Fla.— Senator Ashley Moody continues working to secure long-sought FEMA assistance funds for Florida communities recovering after being hit by major hurricanes. Senator Moody has now secured nearly $2 billion in total funds statewide. Senator Moody secured more than $64 million for Charlotte County covering 28 restoration projects and broke the news today at the county EOC.

chunks.title: VIDEO: Senator Moody Secures Nearly $2 Billion in FEMA Recovery Assistance for Florida Communities Hit by Major Hurricanes - Senator Moody
chunks.text: “Florida has been waiting on essential disaster assistance funds for hurricane recovery since 2017— I’ve been in the Senate for less than a year and a half and have worked hard to bring nearly $2 billion of outstanding FEMA funds back home to Florida. I’ll continue fighting to deliver the federal support Floridians need while making the disaster recovery process more transparent, efficient, and accountable,” said Senator Ashley Moody .

chunks.title: VIDEO: Senator Moody Secures Nearly $2 Billion in FEMA Recovery Assistance for Florida Communities Hit by Major Hurricanes - Senator Moody
chunks.text: Senator Moody secured more than $64 million for 28 projects in Charlotte County. The projects support the restoration of essential infrastructure, including waterways, roads, traffic signal systems, debris removal, and improvements to the Port of Charlotte. These federal investments have played a critical role in the recovery from the impacts of Hurricanes Debby, Helene, Milton, Idalia, and Ian. Additionally, more than $14.4 million has been secured in joint projects including Charlotte County and other counties in the Southwest region. Senator Moody also announced today that more than $57 million has been secured for nearby Lee County and more than $4.2 million for Collier County.

chunks.title: VIDEO: Senator Moody Secures Nearly $2 Billion in FEMA Recovery Assistance for Florida Communities Hit by Major Hurricanes - Senator Moody
chunks.text: Statewide, Senator Moody has secured more than $1.8 billion in FEMA public assistance funding. These grants will be distributed along with the previously announced funds through FEMA’s Public Assistance and Hazard Mitigation Assistance programs to support more than 500 recovery projects across the state. This money is disbursed to the state and local communities for disaster recovery projects. These projects include repairs to educational facilities, restoration of critical infrastructure, debris removal, and costs incurred during emergencies to protect life and property.

chunks.title: VIDEO: Senator Moody Secures Nearly $2 Billion in FEMA Recovery Assistance for Florida Communities Hit by Major Hurricanes - Senator Moody
chunks.text: Senator Moody introduced the  TRACK Act   (Transparency in Recovery Assistance & Claims Knowledge Act) to bring more transparency to the FEMA disaster aid process, which has now been passed into law. The TRACK Act mandates a status tracker on the FEMA website, so victims of a disaster have easily available knowledge and insight of their claim’s progress.

chunks.title: Senator Moody Fights for Affordable Homeownership for Florida Law Enforcement Officers - Senator Moody
chunks.text: Senator Moody Fights for Affordable Homeownership for Florida Law Enforcement Officers - Senator Moody Senator Moody Fights for Affordable Homeownership for Florida Law Enforcement Officers The HELPER Act is a Top Priority for Senator Moody and the First Bill She is Sponsoring as Florida’s Newest U.S. Senator

chunks.title: Senator Moody Fights for Affordable Homeownership for Florida Law Enforcement Officers - Senator Moody
chunks.text: WASHINGTON, D.C. — As a strong supporter of law enforcement, Senator Ashley Moody today filed her first bill to make homeownership more obtainable for Florida heroes. The Homes for Every Local Protector, Educator, and Responder (HELPER) Act would establish a program to provide mortgage assistance to law enforcement officers, firefighters, and other first responders. Primary and secondary teachers would also be eligible for the home loan program with the Federal Housing Administration that would be established through the HELPER Act.

chunks.title: Senator Moody Fights for Affordable Homeownership for Florida Law Enforcement Officers - Senator Moody
chunks.text: Senator Ashley Moody said, “Florida is the most pro law enforcement state in the nation. Over the past six years, while many other states and cities disparaged and cut funding for law enforcement, I fought for raises, bonuses, relocation assistance, and other benefits to show these officers that we value their service. The HELPER Act is the next great step in ensuring these heroes know we appreciate their hard work and sacrifices. It will also help them purchase a home in the community where they serve. As the wife of a law enforcement officer, I see firsthand the sacrifices made each day.

chunks.title: Senator Moody Fights for Affordable Homeownership for Florida Law Enforcement Officers - Senator Moody
chunks.text: Standing up for the LEO community will always be a top priority of mine, and I am proud that my first bill in the U.S. Senate will help them make their dream of homeownership a reality.” Prior to appointment to the U.S. Senate, Senator Moody served as Florida’s Attorney General, a circuit judge, and a federal prosecutor. Senator Moody is also married to a career law enforcement officer. Throughout her career in the judicial system, Senator Moody fought to ensure Florida law enforcement had the tools and support needed to protect and serve. Senator Moody also worked to bridge the gap between law enforcement and the communities they serve:

chunks.title: Senator Moody Fights for Affordable Homeownership for Florida Law Enforcement Officers - Senator Moody
chunks.text: In 2019, Attorney General Moody launched the  Back the Blue campaign  to highlight law enforcement officers, citizens and organizations taking extraordinary steps to forge positive relationships between law enforcement and the communities they serve. In 2020, Attorney General Moody was appointed to  President Donald Trump’s Commission on Law Enforcement and the Administration of Justice . The Commission explored modern issues affecting law enforcement that impact the ability to reduce crime.

chunks.title: Senator Moody Fights for Affordable Homeownership for Florida Law Enforcement Officers - Senator Moody
chunks.text: In 2020, Attorney General Moody announced a new statewide number,  **TIPS , that anyone can call to anonymously report crime. Dialing **TIPS from any cellphone will automatically route the caller to the closest Crime Stoppers office. In 2021, Attorney General Moody started  Be a Florida Hero , a recruitment initiative that encourages jobseekers or law enforcement officers in other states to pursue a law enforcement career in the Sunshine State. chunks.text: WASHINGTON ­­– Congressman Mario Diaz-Balart (FL-25), senior member of the House Committee on Appropriations and Founder and Co-Chair of the House Everglades Caucus, issued the following statement after the passage of America's Water Infrastructure Act of 2018 and the fiscal year 2019 Energy and Water, Legislative Branch, and Military Construction and Veterans Affairs Appropriations Act. America's Water Infrastructure Act of 2018 is a reauthorization of the Water Resources Development Act (WRDA).

chunks.title: Diaz-Balart Votes for EAA Storage Reservoir, Herbert Hoover Dike Funding, Continued Everglades Restoration | Congressman Mario Diaz-Balart
chunks.text: "Today, Congress took another step forward in continued Everglades restoration and protection from flooding and harmful algal blooms in the communities surrounding Lake Okeechobee. The America's Water Infrastructure Act, which authorizes the construction of the EAA Storage Reservoir, is a much-needed solution as Lake Okeechobee and Southern Florida's coasts continue to suffer from algal bloom. The EAA Storage Reservoir has been a top priority for Florida, and I am glad we could work together with our partners at the local and state levels to address the issue in an effective and expedient manner.

chunks.title: Diaz-Balart Votes for EAA Storage Reservoir, Herbert Hoover Dike Funding, Continued Everglades Restoration | Congressman Mario Diaz-Balart
chunks.text: The bill also includes a provision to ensure Lake Okeechobee's water levels coincide with the expedited completion of the Herbert Hoover Dike, reducing the risk of flooding in the surrounding Hendry County communities.

chunks.text: "Similarly, with passage of the Appropriations bill, Southern Florida will continue to see dividends as the bill contains provisions that further the expedited completion of the dike, as well as Everglades restoration. These funds, combined with the $514 million I helped secure this July from the hurricane relief and recovery funding package , are anticipated to complete this much-needed rehabilitation project by 2022-2023. I look forward to this achievement being reached and am proud to have had a part in securing the necessary funding from Congress.

chunks.title: Díaz-Balart Votes to Extend Haiti TPS | Congressman Mario Diaz-Balart
chunks.text: “Since returning to office, President Trump proved that to end the border crisis, all that needed to be done was to enforce the rule of law. I’ve long supported strong border security measures, including as an original sponsor and author of H.R. 2, Secure the Border Act, the most comprehensive and conservative border security bill ever. chunks.text: Haiti continues to face severe instability driven by natural disasters, corruption, and widespread violence, making it extraordinarily difficult for its people to live safely. chunks.title: Diaz-Balart Statement on TPS for Venezuelans | Congressman Mario Diaz-Balart
chunks.text: " The Biden Administration's decision to provide TPS to Venezuelan nationals in Florida does not change the protections that were already provided to them under Deferred Enforced Departure (DED) during the Trump Administration. However, the Biden Administration has indicated that Venezuelans in the United States should still apply for TPS in case it decides to let the DED protections for Venezuelans expire. Therefore, rather than Venezuelans automatically being protected by DED, as they were under the Trump Administration, they will need to apply for TPS and pay a fee, which was not required under DED.

chunks.title: Diaz-Balart Statement on TPS for Venezuelans | Congressman Mario Diaz-Balart
chunks.text: "Two weeks ago, I asked the Biden Administration for clarification on the status of DED for Venezuelans, particularly the procedures for obtaining work authorization. chunks.title: Diaz-Balart: Forcing TPS Beneficiaries to Leave U.S. Would Be Detrimental | Congressman Mario Diaz-Balart
chunks.text: "Similar to my disagreement with the decision to end TPS for Nicaraguan nationals, I am strongly opposed to and disagree with the decision to end TPS for Haitian nationals living in the United States. Almost eight years later, Haiti remains in total disarray and still requires much rebuilding. These individuals are established, respected members of our communities who have made significant contributions, and I urge the administration to reconsider its decision regarding Haitian and Nicaraguan nationals."

Faster care, real mental health support, and full accountability at the VA — that’s what our veterans have earned. SECURE BORDERS & A LEGAL IMMIGRATION SYSTEM

chunks.title: On The Issues - Te Brown For Congress
chunks.text: A nation must have secure borders and a fair, lawful immigration system. I support securing our southern border, enforcing our immigration laws, and prioritizing the removal of criminals and those who pose a threat to public safety. At the same time, we should create a clear, lawful process for people who have earned the right to remain, while ending policies that encourage illegal immigration and ensuring that those who follow the rules are not left behind. Faith, family, and freedom are the foundation of America. Religious liberty, parental rights, the Second Amendment, and the Constitution itself are under attack — and they’re worth fighting for.

chunks.title: On The Issues - Te Brown For Congress
chunks.text: For 15 years, Washington has told Haitian families in South Florida that their status was temporary, and for 15 years nothing changed. During that time, the situation in Haiti has only worsened, and many community members have built businesses, raised families, staffed hospitals, and created institutions the rest of us depend on. Put simply, that is not a temporary population, and the community has earned better than a deportation notice.

chunks.title: On The Issues - Te Brown For Congress
chunks.text: In Congress, I will fight for an earned path to citizenship. Earned: a steady work history, taxes paid, a clean record, a full background check. Not amnesty, and not a cut ahead of anyone who waited in line. A Republican Congress did this in 1998 with the Haitian Refugee Immigration Fairness Act, and it was right then. Those who have worked, paid taxes, built our communities, and embodied the American experience should not be cast aside, but welcomed as who they are: Haitian-Americans.

chunks.title: On The Issues - Te Brown For Congress
chunks.text: I won’t pretend, either, that the other side doesn’t matter. No immigration bill can fix the status of Port-Au-Prince and Haiti. I will work to end the South Florida weapons pipeline to Port-Au-Prince, and back the effort to rebuild, because nobody wants a stable Haiti more than those forced to leave it.

chunks.title: The People First Agenda - Te Brown For Congress
chunks.text: The People First Agenda - Te Brown For Congress Putting People Before Politics. Delivering Results That Matter. A bold agenda focused on lowering the cost of living, making housing and childcare more affordable, protecting seniors and veterans, creating jobs, protecting the healthcare system, strengthening communities, and putting families first. 1. Affordability & Homeownership — Lower the barriers to buying a home, build more affordable housing, and address the cost of living. 2. Healthcare That Works — Increase transparency, lower prescription and healthcare costs, and protect patients from unnecessary costs.

chunks.title: The People First Agenda - Te Brown For Congress
chunks.text: 3. Jobs & Economic Opportunity — Support small businesses, attract manufacturing, and create good-paying jobs in the district. 4. Infrastructure & Resilience — Invest in roads, bridges, water systems, drainage, and infrastructure that keeps South Florida moving. 5. Protecting Seniors & Veterans — Protect Social Security and Medicare while making sure veterans receive the services they’ve earned. 6. Safe & Strong Communities — Support law enforcement, address crime, and make communities safer. 7. Education & Opportunity — Expand educational choices and make sure children have pathways to careers, trades, college, or entrepreneurship.

chunks.title: The People First Agenda - Te Brown For Congress
chunks.text: 8. Accountability in Washington — Make government live within its means, eliminate waste, and demand measurable results Your concerns are not just messages—they’re the issues I intend to fight to address. Send me your concerns, ideas, and priorities. Together, we can build a People’s First Agenda that delivers results. Email me your concerns and ideas at info@tmbrownforcongress.com

chunks.title: Meet Te Brown - Te Brown For Congress
chunks.text: Te Mayonna Brown is the Republican nominee for Florida’s 24th Congressional District. A successful businesswoman, educator, and trailblazing real estate developer, she has spent her career building stronger communities, creating opportunities, and helping families achieve the American Dream. As a woman real estate developer, Te has transformed neighborhoods through affordable housing and economic investment. Her work has given her firsthand experience solving real-world challenges, creating jobs, and helping communities grow.

chunks.title: Meet Te Brown - Te Brown For Congress
chunks.text: Te also understands the importance of education. As a former teacher, she believes every child deserves access to a quality education and that parents—not government bureaucrats—should have the freedom to choose the best educational path for their children. She is a strong advocate for school choice and policies that put students and families first.

chunks.title: Meet Te Brown - Te Brown For Congress
chunks.text: Now, Te is taking her experience as a builder, educator, and entrepreneur to Washington. She isn’t a career politician—she’s a proven leader who knows how to get results. She is committed to fighting for stronger wage growth, affordable housing, lower costs for working families, safer communities, and policies that encourage businesses to grow and create better-paying jobs. Te believes America is strongest when government is limited, communities are safe, the economy is growing, and every family has the opportunity to succeed through hard work.

chunks.title: Meet Te Brown - Te Brown For Congress
chunks.text: As your next representative in Congress, Te Mayonna Brown will be a strong voice for economic growth, public safety, fiscal responsibility, individual freedom, and common-sense leadership. She will work every day to protect taxpayers, support small businesses, strengthen families, and ensure the next generation has even greater opportunities than the last. Together, we can build a stronger Florida, a stronger economy, and a brighter future for the families of Florida’s 24th Congressional District.

chunks.title: News – Te Brown For Congress
chunks.text: Check back soon for the latest updates and announcements from the campaign. Subscribe to our newsletter for the latest campaign updates. No upcoming events to show at this time.

chunks.title: Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: By providing your cell phone number you consent to receive periodic campaign updates from Oliver Gilbert for Congress. Texting & data rates may apply. Reply "STOP" to stop texts. Reply "HELP" for help. I consent to receive SMS messages from Oliver Gilbert for Congress. Message & data rates may apply, Reply "STOP" to stop texts, reply "help" for help Rooted in Miami Gardens and shaped by the people who raised him, taught him, and stood by him, Oliver Gilbert is running to give back to the community that made him who he is. Raised in Miami Gardens, educated in local public schools, and shaped by a lifetime of service to his community, he is running to build a stronger future for South Florida.

chunks.title: Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: His story is one of faith, perseverance, and service — from supporting himself as a college student and riding the bus to law school, to leading his growing hometown as Mayor and bringing safer neighborhoods, more parks, real economic growth, to fighting as a County Commissioner for better public transit, housing people can afford, and economic growth that benefits the entire region — his focus has always been on creating stronger neighborhoods, more resilient communities, and a better future for working families. At every step, his purpose has remained the same: to bring opportunity home and build a South Florida where every family has a fair shot.

chunks.title: Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: They want to get to work without losing half their day. They want to see a doctor without dreading the bill. They want their kids to inherit an economy that rewards effort. A two-hour commute isn’t a transit problem. It’s a family problem, a cost problem, and a life problem. Nobody should wait until it’s too late to see a doctor because of the bill. Coverage isn’t a luxury. It’s a foundation. Small businesses and working families built South Florida. They deserve a federal government that builds with them — not around them. and build a brighter future for everyone in South Florida Eliminate Income Taxes for Working Families

chunks.title: Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: Startup grants and affordable financing to get your idea off the ground. The SBA Growth Line offers low-interest loans to help you scale up. A strengthened SBA 504 program makes buying property and expanding easier. Employee ownership and profit-sharing incentives that help workers build wealth. Less paperwork, simpler reporting, and faster approvals for small businesses. Small Business Opportunity Zones that revitalize local commercial corridors. Oliver is relying on the grassroots support of voters like you. Will you make a secure online donation today? This is the most meaningful endorsement I could ask for.

chunks.title: Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: Congresswoman Wilson has fought for this community for decades, the last 15 years in Congress doing the hard work to move our community and country forward and she does not give her word lightly. She knows better than anyone what’s needed in Washington. I grew up right here in South Florida, in Miami Gardens. I know what families here are up against, because I have lived it. Rent that eats half a paycheck. Healthcare people cannot afford. A commute that swallows the day. I am running to change that. Not with promises, but with work. I am humbled to have her trust, and I will work every day to be worthy of it.

chunks.title: On the Issues - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: On the Issues - Oliver Gilbert for Congress Gas is $5 a gallon, rent is half your paycheck, and every trip to the grocery store gets more expensive. For far too many neighbors, this has been the reality for far too long. Oliver Gilbert lived these challenges growing up in Miami Gardens, working his way through college and law school, and leading our city as Mayor and County Commissioner.

chunks.title: On the Issues - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: What do President Trump and Washington Republicans do to help during these tough times? They spend your money on a war you didn’t ask for, didn’t vote for, and don’t need. They build a billion dollar ballroom for the Mar-a-Lago crowd. And they even use your own money to lie right to your face, spending millions on TV ads to deny the truth and divide our communities. South Florida families have had enough. It’s time to Put People First. We’re the richest country on earth, but we send billions of dollars to other countries so they can afford universal healthcare. How does that make sense? In Congress, Oliver will fight for a pathway to ensure that healthcare is a right for every American.

chunks.title: On the Issues - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: Eliminate Income Taxes for Working Families Families who are working hard to make ends meet shouldn’t have to carry the same tax burden as billionaires. The IRS should be spending more time auditing the ultra-wealthy than scrutinizing an Uber driver’s gas deduction. Oliver supports common sense tax policies indexed to what families in our communities actually earn, so that relief reaches the people who need it most and keeps money in working people’s hands.

chunks.title: On the Issues - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: Our government has shamefully spent billions ripping families apart. They said ICE would only target criminals, but every day more and more hardworking people are being arrested and deported, often leaving young children behind to fend for themselves or leaving the only country they’ve ever known. It’s time to end funding for these shameful deportation policies and redirect that investment where it belongs: into our communities.

chunks.title: On the Issues - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: Countries around the world have made universal childcare a reality. As a father, Oliver knows the challenges families are facing every day. In Washington, he will redirect spending toward our children and families, so that the resources no longer being wasted on mass deportations start building something that actually lasts. In Congress, Oliver will fight to secure the federal funding needed to ensure the job gets done, and that our residents get the transit solutions they’ve been promised for decades.

chunks.title: On the Issues - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: Oliver will fight in Washington to reinvest in job training, especially in high-paying technical fields that can’t easily be taken away by AI, and to strengthen support for entrepreneurs and small business owners. America should not only be the best place in the world to work. It should be the best place in the world to start a business. Every student deserves a pathway to purpose. The BUILD Act prepares students for the economy of tomorrow by connecting education to real careers, expanding apprenticeships, supporting teachers, rewarding innovation, and building the workforce America needs to compete.

chunks.title: On the Issues - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: Every person with a lifelong disability deserves healthcare, a safe home, meaningful relationships, and the support to live with dignity throughout every stage of life. The HOME Act lowers monthly housing costs without weakening lending standards — helping responsible families own a home, build generational wealth, and gain long-term financial stability.

chunks.title: My Story - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: I grew up here. I went to school here. I served here. And every step of that journey is the reason I’m running. I was raised in Miami Gardens by two people who didn’t always see the world the same way. My mom was a Seventh-day Adventist teacher. My dad was a Baptist preacher. And in our house, I learned something early: people don’t have to agree on everything to love each other, to build a life together, to raise a family together. They respected each other. They built something. That stayed with me.

chunks.title: My Story - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: Parkview Elementary. Parkway Middle. Miami Norland Senior High School. Every year of K through 12 happened right here. The teachers who taught me, the neighbors who watched me grow up, the friends who became family — they’re the reason I’m running, and they’re who I’m running for. Florida A&M was my first real test. There were nights I lived out of my car. The work ethic and faith I brought from home are the only reasons I made it through. I learned that hardship isn’t something to perform — it’s something you live through, and what you do after defines you.

chunks.title: My Story - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: Law school meant a commute. I’d ride the 27 bus all the way down 27th Avenue to the Martin Luther King Metrorail station, then take the train to Coral Gables for class at the University of Miami School of Law. Some nights I’d get back late. And my dad would meet me at the MLK station. Every time. And he’d ask me one question. He wasn’t asking for himself. He wanted the knowledge to come back home. That question shaped everything I’ve done since.

chunks.title: My Story - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: I had the honor of serving as Mayor of my hometown for eight years. We worked on what mattered: safer neighborhoods, more parks, real economic growth, the kind of community policing that builds trust instead of breaking it. In 2020, Miami Gardens was named an All-America City — the first time in our history. I’m proud of that. But I’m more proud of what made it possible: a community that decided to invest in itself.

chunks.title: My Story - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: On the County Commission, I’ve focused on a new goal: Make Miami-Dade County a truly world-class community. To get there, we have to overhaul our transportation system, which is why I’ve led bold initiatives to build up density along our transit corridors, creating partnerships that will fund rapid transit expansion and lead to more affordable housing in the neighborhoods that need it the most. What I’ve seen serving this community is simple. People want the same things. Good schools. Healthcare they can actually access. A commute that doesn’t take their life from them. A small business that can compete. A future their kids can build on.

chunks.title: My Story - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: That’s what this campaign is about. Not running against anyone. Running toward something. Building a future that works for everyone, across South Florida.

chunks.title: BUILD Act - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: Every student deserves a pathway to purpose. The BUILD Act prepares students for the economy of tomorrow by connecting education to real careers, expanding apprenticeships, supporting teachers, rewarding innovation, and building the workforce America needs to compete. In-Demand Careers Stronger Workforce. Stronger America. America cannot compete in tomorrow's economy with yesterday's education system. The BUILD Act recognizes that human capacity is infrastructure. Investing in people strengthens our economy, grows small businesses, and improves national competitiveness. Skills and credentials create higher-paying career paths and increase lifetime earning potential.

chunks.title: BUILD Act - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: Expanding access to education and training opens doors for every student and every community. Nine ways the BUILD Act builds America's workforce. Tap any item to expand. Federal incentive grants reward school districts that develop career pathways in AI, cybersecurity, healthcare, advanced manufacturing, logistics, infrastructure, entrepreneurship, aerospace, and the skilled trades. Every student graduates college ready, trade ready, entrepreneurially ready, or workforce ready through certifications, dual enrollment, apprenticeships, and career pathways.

chunks.title: BUILD Act - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: Educational assistance for trade school, college, graduate school, and professional school in exchange for service in designated national priority industries. Enhanced Public Service Loan Forgiveness Expand and modernize loan forgiveness for teachers, nurses, first responders, military personnel, public defenders, and other public service professionals. Competitive federal grants reward districts that embrace innovation, workforce readiness, measurable outcomes, and industry partnerships. Enhanced grants for districts investing in teacher compensation, teacher retention, mentoring, and professional development. Teachers are America's first responders for the future.

chunks.title: BUILD Act - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: Accomplished professionals including engineers, physicians, scientists, entrepreneurs, artists, musicians, architects, attorneys, journalists, software developers, skilled trades professionals, veterans, and researchers may co-teach advanced courses for one semester. Certified teachers remain the teacher of record while BUILD Fellows contribute real-world expertise. National recognition and additional grant eligibility for school districts demonstrating exceptional workforce preparation and student success. Increase funding for Historically Black Colleges and Universities and other colleges that provide education to underserved communities. Higher wages create higher tax revenues.

chunks.title: BUILD Act - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: More apprenticeships reduce workforce shortages. Public-private partnerships maximize taxpayer investment. Reward results instead of imposing mandates. Teachers are America's first responders for the future. Police officers respond when communities are in crisis. Firefighters respond when buildings are burning. Emergency medical personnel respond when lives are in immediate danger. Teachers respond before those crises ever occur by preparing the next generation with the knowledge, discipline, critical thinking, and character that strengthen our communities and our economy. Every student deserves a pathway to purpose.

chunks.title: BUILD Business Act - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: BUILD Business Act - Oliver Gilbert for Congress America should not only be the best place in the world to work. It should be the best place in the world to start a business. Small businesses are the backbone of the American economy. The BUILD Business Act modernizes the Small Business Administration by expanding access to capital, reducing barriers to entrepreneurship, and helping more Americans start, grow, and expand successful businesses. Too many entrepreneurs have the talent and determination to succeed but cannot access the capital needed to get started. The BUILD Business Act closes that gap by pairing affordable financing with mentorship, accountability, and streamlined government.

chunks.title: BUILD Business Act - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: Eleven concrete actions to help Americans start, grow, and expand small businesses. Tap any item to expand. Create the American Small Business Grant Program providing grants of $5,000 to $25,000 for equipment, inventory, software, licensing, insurance, lease deposits, and other startup costs. Goal: Give entrepreneurs access to capital before debt becomes necessary. Establish the SBA Growth Line offering low interest loans, generally from 0% to 2%, with deferred repayment. Goal: Help growing businesses scale without being overwhelmed by early debt.

chunks.title: BUILD Business Act - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: Strengthen the SBA 7(a) program by increasing federal guarantees, reducing borrower fees, simplifying approvals, speeding processing, and expanding lending in underserved communities. Strengthen the SBA 504 program by expanding funding, modernizing eligibility, speeding project approvals, and creating a new 504 Express Expansion track for established businesses creating jobs. Provide enhanced financing incentives for businesses that establish employee ownership and profit-sharing programs. Goal: Help workers build wealth alongside the businesses they help build. Combine startup grants, affordable financing, technical assistance, and contracting opportunities in targeted commercial corridors.

chunks.title: BUILD Business Act - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: Goal: Revitalize communities through local entrepreneurship. Reduce lender risk by covering the initial portion of losses on qualifying startup loans. Goal: Encourage more private lending to promising entrepreneurs. Create one digital portal for grants, loans, mentoring, technical assistance, and contracting opportunities. Goal: Make government easier to navigate. Expand Mentorship and Business Development Partner with universities, chambers of commerce, Small Business Development Centers, experienced business mentors, minority business organizations, and local economic development agencies.

chunks.title: BUILD Business Act - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: Publish annual reports measuring business creation, job creation, survival rates, loan performance, and taxpayer return on investment. Simplify procurement and help more small businesses compete for government contracts. Goal: Create reliable customers, not just affordable financing. Reduce paperwork, simplify reporting requirements, coordinate permitting where possible, and expand digital services. Goal: Let entrepreneurs spend more time growing businesses. Opening your first restaurant? Access startup grants and affordable financing. Buying your first commercial building? A strengthened SBA 504 program makes expansion easier.

chunks.title: BUILD Business Act - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: Growing a construction, trucking, retail, or service business? A stronger SBA 7(a) program helps finance hiring and equipment. Veteran, first-time entrepreneur, or business owner in an underserved community? Benefit from expanded mentoring and streamlined access to capital. Employee? Expanded ownership incentives create more opportunities to build wealth. The BUILD Business Act shifts federal policy from simply recruiting employers to creating more of them. When small businesses succeed, communities create jobs, families build wealth, neighborhoods become stronger, and America's economy grows from the ground up. Improve five-year business survival rates.

chunks.title: BUILD Business Act - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: Expand lending in underserved communities. Grow federal contracts awarded to small businesses. Increase locally owned businesses and local job creation. Require business plans for grant applicants. Maintain prudent underwriting standards for loans. Publish annual audits and performance reports. Investigate and prosecute fraud aggressively.

chunks.title: CARE Act - Lifelong Care and Community for Americans with Disabilities - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: CARE Act - Lifelong Care and Community for Americans with Disabilities - Oliver Gilbert for Congress A Full Life. A Secure Future. A Promise That Lasts. Every person with a lifelong disability deserves healthcare, a safe home, meaningful relationships, and the support to live with dignity throughout every stage of life. For millions of families, the hardest question is not what happens today. It is what happens tomorrow.

chunks.title: CARE Act - Lifelong Care and Community for Americans with Disabilities - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: Parents of children with intellectual, developmental, and other lifelong disabilities often spend decades serving as caregivers, advocates, benefits experts, transportation coordinators, housing planners, and emergency responders. They hold together a system that was never designed to work as one system. When a child becomes an adult, families can face separate rules for Medicaid, Medicare, Social Security, housing, employment services, transportation, and community programming. A parent may have to contact multiple agencies just to keep basic services in place. Then comes the question no family should have to face alone: What happens when the parent becomes sick, grows older, or dies?

chunks.title: CARE Act - Lifelong Care and Community for Americans with Disabilities - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: Too often, the answer is a crisis. Housing is disrupted. Caregivers disappear. Benefits lapse. Siblings are asked to take over without preparation. Adults who have lived in the community may face isolation or unnecessary institutional placement. That is not a system of care. It is a system of uncertainty. The CARE Act creates a comprehensive federal framework for lifelong care and community living. It brings existing programs together, fills the gaps between them, and ensures that every eligible person has one coordinated plan for life. No person should lose healthcare, housing, caregiving, or community because a parent can no longer provide care.

chunks.title: CARE Act - Lifelong Care and Community for Americans with Disabilities - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: The CARE Act is built around eight commitments . Tap any item to expand. Every eligible person will have one federally certified CARE Advocate beginning during the transition to adulthood and continuing throughout life. The CARE Advocate becomes the family's single point of contact and coordinates services across Medicaid, Medicare, Social Security, housing, healthcare, transportation, employment, education, and community programs. What it means One person responsible for making sure the whole system works together.

chunks.title: CARE Act - Lifelong Care and Community for Americans with Disabilities - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: Eligible individuals will receive timely access to necessary home and community-based services, including personal assistance, nursing, therapies, behavioral healthcare, transportation, respite care, supported employment, day services, residential support, and emergency backup care. What it means Community care should be dependable, not something families wait years to receive.

chunks.title: CARE Act - Lifelong Care and Community for Americans with Disabilities - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: The CARE Act will expand accessible housing modeled after successful efforts such as Casa Familia, including supported apartments, small shared homes, mixed-income communities, independent living options, and higher-support residences. Housing funding and care funding will be coordinated instead of treated as unrelated programs. What it means The goal is not simply a bed. The goal is a home and a community.

chunks.title: CARE Act - Lifelong Care and Community for Americans with Disabilities - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: Community Belonging Grants will support programs that create real relationships and full community participation. That includes models similar to Friendship Circle, Best Buddies, Special Olympics, faith-based inclusion programs, arts, recreation, volunteer service, peer mentoring, and civic engagement. What it means A full life includes friends, places to go, people who know your name, and opportunities to contribute.

chunks.title: CARE Act - Lifelong Care and Community for Americans with Disabilities - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: Beginning in adolescence, each participant and family will create a Lifelong Support Plan covering housing, healthcare, communication needs, transportation, employment, daily support, emergency care, financial planning, future caregivers, and supported decision-making. The plan will follow the individual and be updated over time. What it means The transition after a parent's death should never begin with strangers trying to reconstruct a person's life. The CARE Act expands respite care, caregiver training, mental health support, sibling planning, legal and financial guidance, emergency caregiver networks, and transition assistance.

chunks.title: CARE Act - Lifelong Care and Community for Americans with Disabilities - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: What it means Parents should be allowed to be parents, not unpaid administrators of a broken system. The plan invests in direct support professionals through better reimbursement, competitive wages, training, career ladders, benefits, recruitment, retention, and emergency staffing. What it means A promise of care means little if there is no one available to provide it. The CARE Act will make assistive technology part of the basic support plan, including communication devices, smart-home systems, wearable health tools, remote monitoring chosen by the individual, adaptive robotics, mobility technology, accessible transportation, and digital care coordination.

chunks.title: CARE Act - Lifelong Care and Community for Americans with Disabilities - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: What it means Technology should increase independence and safety without replacing human connection or personal choice. The CARE Advocate is the practical center of the plan. This person will not replace a parent, guardian, caregiver, doctor, or benefits agency. The advocate will make sure they are communicating and working from one coordinated plan. Helps the individual and family create and update the Lifelong Support Plan. Coordinates applications, renewals, and transitions involving Medicaid, Medicare, Social Security, housing, employment, and transportation. Organizes annual meetings with the individual, family, caregivers, providers, and appropriate agencies.

chunks.title: CARE Act - Lifelong Care and Community for Americans with Disabilities - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: Maintains an emergency and successor-care plan. Tracks deadlines and prevents avoidable gaps in benefits or services. Helps resolve disputes and escalates urgent needs when agencies fail to respond. Monitors actual quality of life, not merely whether forms were completed. Remains accountable to the individual and respects supported decision-making, privacy, choice, and independence. Federal agencies will retain their legal authority over eligibility and benefits. The CARE Advocate will have statutory coordination authority, access to participating agencies with the individual's consent, and the ability to require timely responses and elevate unresolved cases.

chunks.title: CARE Act - Lifelong Care and Community for Americans with Disabilities - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: Every participant will have one secure, portable Lifelong Support Plan recognized across participating programs. The individual must be at the center of that plan, with family and trusted supporters involved according to the individual's preferences and legal rights. Communication preferences and assistive technology Education, employment, volunteering, and meaningful daytime activity Friendships, recreation, faith, culture, and community participation Supported decision-making or guardianship arrangements Social Security, representative payee, ABLE account, trust, and financial planning Successor caregivers and the transition when parents can no longer provide care

chunks.title: CARE Act - Lifelong Care and Community for Americans with Disabilities - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: The CARE Act will establish continuous coverage and coordinated care for people with qualifying lifelong disabilities. Medicaid will remain the principal payer for long-term services and supports. Medicare will cover eligible medical services. Social Security will provide income support. The CARE Advocate will make those systems function as one plan instead of separate bureaucracies. Prevent unnecessary interruptions in Medicaid for people with permanent qualifying disabilities. Provide Medicaid wraparound coverage for services Medicare does not cover. Expand access to Medicaid Buy-In so people can work without losing essential care.

chunks.title: CARE Act - Lifelong Care and Community for Americans with Disabilities - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: Require coverage of emergency backup caregiving and transition support. Reduce repetitive paperwork and duplicative disability reviews where the condition is permanent. Protect continuity when an individual moves between communities or across state lines. 06 / Building More Places Like Casa Familia The CARE Act will create a national Community Living Capital Fund to help nonprofit organizations, local governments, housing providers, and families build or preserve accessible community housing. The program will coordinate HUD housing resources, federal tax incentives, local land, nonprofit investment, and Medicaid-funded services.

chunks.title: CARE Act - Lifelong Care and Community for Americans with Disabilities - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: Federal support should be flexible enough to help create different options because adults with disabilities do not all need or want the same living arrangement. Small homes shared by a limited number of residents Supported apartments with staff available on site Mixed-income and mixed-ability developments Independent apartments with visiting support Residences designed for people with more significant medical or behavioral needs The standard must be dignity, safety, individual choice, and meaningful connection to the surrounding community. Community living cannot become institutional care with a nicer sign out front.

chunks.title: CARE Act - Lifelong Care and Community for Americans with Disabilities - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: One coordinated promise replaces a patchwork of disconnected programs. Here is the difference for families living it every day. One CARE Advocate coordinates the entire plan. Community services can depend on a waiting list. Necessary lifelong supports are guaranteed on a timely basis. Succession and emergency planning begin during adolescence. Housing, services, transportation, and community programming are coordinated. Parents worry about what happens when they die. A successor-care plan, stable housing, and a support team are already in place. Success is measured by safety, health, independence, relationships, purpose, and belonging. 08 / How the Federal Government Will Work Together

chunks.title: CARE Act - Lifelong Care and Community for Americans with Disabilities - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: The CARE Act does not pretend that one existing agency can do everything. It gives each agency a clear responsibility and creates one coordinated system around the individual. Oversees the CARE Advocate Corps, national standards, community inclusion grants, family support, and quality-of-life accountability. Funds long-term services and supports, personal care, residential services, therapies, respite, transportation, and care coordination. Supports accessible housing construction, rental assistance, nonprofit development, and community living options. Administers SSI, Disabled Adult Child benefits, income support, and representative payee services.

chunks.title: CARE Act - Lifelong Care and Community for Americans with Disabilities - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: Provides medical coverage for eligible participants, coordinated with Medicaid wraparound services. Support transition, workforce preparation, supported employment, and opportunities to contribute. Expands accessible and dependable transportation and future mobility solutions. States, Counties, and Community Partners Deliver services locally and develop housing, programs, and care networks tailored to their communities. 09 / Protecting Choice and Preventing Abuse

chunks.title: CARE Act - Lifelong Care and Community for Americans with Disabilities - Oliver Gilbert for Congress
chunks.text: A stronger care system must also protect the rights of the people it serves. The CARE Act will include independent oversight, transparent reporting, background and training standards, accessible complaint procedures, protection against abuse and financial exploitation, and regular review of restrictive guardianships. chunks.title: Moskowitz Leads Effort to Extend National Flood Insurance Program and Deliver More Certainty to Florida Homeowners and Businesses
chunks.text: WASHINGTON, DC — With the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) facing imminent expiration, Congressman Jared Moskowitz (D-FL-23) is leading his colleagues to extend the program through December 31, 2026. The NFIP is currently set to expire at 11:59pm on September 30, 2025, but his bill would save it from expiration by extending the program through the end of 2026, significantly longer than typical, shorter-term extensions passed by Congress.

chunks.title: Moskowitz Leads Effort to Extend National Flood Insurance Program and Deliver More Certainty to Florida Homeowners and Businesses
chunks.text: The bipartisan National Flood Insurance Program Authorization Extension Act is also led in the U.S. House by Reps. Troy Carter (D-LA-02), Cleo Fields (D-LA-06), Julia Letlow (R-LA-05), and Mike Ezell (R-MS-04) and in the U.S. Senate by Sens. Bill Cassidy (R-LA) and John Kennedy (R-LA).

chunks.title: Moskowitz Leads Effort to Extend National Flood Insurance Program and Deliver More Certainty to Florida Homeowners and Businesses
chunks.text: “With hurricane season around the corner, Florida homeowners and businesses deserve certainty that the flood insurance policies they’ve paid into will be there when disaster strikes,” said Congressman Moskowitz. “The NFIP needs reform to lower costs for policyholders and be kept solvent, but it’s too important to let lapse. As Congress works towards long-term solutions that’ll save the NFIP, I’m urging my colleagues to join us in extending this lifeline and delivering our communities the security they’re counting on.”

chunks.title: Moskowitz Leads Effort to Extend National Flood Insurance Program and Deliver More Certainty to Florida Homeowners and Businesses
chunks.text: Managed by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), the NFIP provides flood insurance to homeowners and businesses to reduce the financial impact of flooding. It helps protect residents from devastating financial losses due to flood damage, encourages responsible development in flood-prone areas, and supports rebuilding efforts after disasters.

chunks.title: Moskowitz Leads Effort to Extend National Flood Insurance Program and Deliver More Certainty to Florida Homeowners and Businesses
chunks.text: More than five million policyholders—including more than 1.7 million in Florida—look to the NFIP as a lifeline for recovering and rebuilding after disaster. Failing to reauthorize the NFIP could delay claims payments and create market instability. It also means that new policies could not be issued, existing policies could not be renewed, and real estate transactions in flood-prone areas could stall. With Congress having passed 33 short-term authorization extensions over the past decade alone, the NFIP Authorization Extension Act would secure the NFIP for significantly longer than other recent efforts.

chunks.title: Moskowitz Leads Effort to Extend National Flood Insurance Program and Deliver More Certainty to Florida Homeowners and Businesses
chunks.text: Moskowitz has long advocated for reforms to the insurance market that will lower the high costs Floridians face. Last Congress, he introduced legislation to help stabilize the insurance market and lower costs for homeowners by allowing the federal government to guarantee part of the insurance cost for homeowners when disaster strikes. Earlier this Congress, he introduced bipartisan legislation to allow homeowners to set up tax-free “READY” accounts for disaster preparedness.

chunks.title: Moskowitz Leads Effort to Extend National Flood Insurance Program and Deliver More Certainty to Florida Homeowners and Businesses
chunks.text: Before entering Congress, Moskowitz served as Florida’s Director of Emergency Management from 2019-2021. In this role, Moskowitz oversaw disaster response and recovery for the DeSantis Administration for major events like the COVID-19 pandemic and the Category 5 Hurricane Michael.

chunks.title: Moskowitz Leads Effort to Extend National Flood Insurance Program and Deliver More Certainty to Florida Homeowners and Businesses
chunks.text: Since coming to Congress, Moskowitz has been a leading voice for fully funding FEMA, keeping emergency response nonpartisan, and enacting commonsense reforms to bolster federal emergency management, like his bipartisan FEMA Independence Act to remove FEMA from the Department of Homeland Security and reinstate it as an independent Cabinet agency reporting directly to the President. He has served as co-chair of the Bipartisan Congressional Disaster Preparedness and Recovery Caucus. chunks.title: Moskowitz Reintroduces Legislation to Reduce Homeowners Insurance Costs for Florida Families
chunks.text: Moskowitz Reintroduces Legislation to Reduce Homeowners Insurance Costs for Florida Families Moskowitz Reintroduces Legislation to Reduce Homeowners Insurance Costs for Florida Families WASHINGTON, DC — Today, Congressman Jared Moskowitz (D-FL-23) reintroduced his Natural Disaster Risk Reinsurance Act , legislation designed to lower homeowners’ insurance premiums, help families afford to stay in their homes, and stabilize Florida’s collapsing insurance market.

chunks.title: Moskowitz Reintroduces Legislation to Reduce Homeowners Insurance Costs for Florida Families
chunks.text: Florida currently faces the highest average homeowners insurance premiums in the country, driven mainly by rising reinsurance costs. Because insurers purchase increasingly expensive reinsurance to avoid the “risk of ruin” after major storms, those costs are directly passed down to the homeowners. This cycle pushes premiums to unaffordable levels and drives insurers out of the state altogether. “Insurance costs are crushing Florida families, and they deserve real relief — not excuses,” said Congressman Moskowitz. “This bill tackles the root of the problem by lowering reinsurance costs so insurers can lower premiums. It’s long overdue relief for families just trying to stay in their homes.”

chunks.title: Moskowitz Reintroduces Legislation to Reduce Homeowners Insurance Costs for Florida Families
chunks.text: Under the bill, the federal government would: Create a catastrophic reinsurance backstop so insurers can lower premiums and avoid “risk of ruin” after major disasters. Issue post-event bonds when losses exceed a state’s reinsurance cap, with states repaying the bonds over ten years through a temporary surcharge only if a catastrophic event occurs. Allow states to opt in voluntarily and apply the backstop to a broad range of disasters, including hurricanes, severe storms, wildfires, earthquakes, and more.

chunks.title: Moskowitz Reintroduces Legislation to Reduce Homeowners Insurance Costs for Florida Families
chunks.text: Independent estimates show the legislation could reduce insurance rates by roughly 25%, saving the average Florida homeowner about $1,500 in the first year alone. The measure is budget-neutral, with no upfront federal cost, and applies to a wide range of disasters.

chunks.title: Moskowitz Reintroduces Legislation to Reduce Homeowners Insurance Costs for Florida Families
chunks.text: Moskowitz first introduced this legislation during his first term in 2023 in response to Florida’s rapidly escalating insurance crisis. In the years since, premiums have continued to rise, insurers have exited the market in droves, and Florida’s families have struggled to find affordable coverage. The Natural Disaster Risk Reinsurance Act is intended to give states a tool to lower costs, keep insurers in the marketplace, and protect families against financial hardship after major disasters.

chunks.title: Moskowitz Reintroduces Legislation to Reduce Homeowners Insurance Costs for Florida Families
chunks.text: Before entering Congress, Moskowitz served as Florida’s Director of Emergency Management from 2019–2021, overseeing disaster response for events such as the COVID-19 pandemic and Hurricane Michael. Since coming to Congress, he has worked to strengthen disaster preparedness, support affordable insurance reform, and reduce costs for Florida homeowners.
