chunks.title: Wancito Francius for State Representative District 108
chunks.text: The Nathan Emmanuel Francius Autism Support and Resources Act This Act shall be known and may be cited as the "Nathan Emmanuel Francius Autism Support and Resources Act." (a) The Legislature finds that Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) affects many Florida children, requiring specialized resources and interventions for their development and success. (b) The Legislature recognizes the critical need for tools, programs, and professional support to address the unique needs of children with ASD. (c) The Legislature intends to allocate funding for schools and professionals to enhance support for children with ASD.

chunks.title: Wancito Francius for State Representative District 108
chunks.text: (a) "Autism Spectrum Evaluation (ASE) Program" means a program providing tools, resources, and interventions for children with Autism Spectrum Disorder. (b) "Registered Behavior Technician (RBT)" means a paraprofessional certified in behavioral health, specializing in working with children diagnosed with ASD. (c) "Eligible Schools" means public or private schools in Florida operating for at least two years. (a) The Department of Education (DOE) shall allocate $3,000,000 for Autism Spectrum Evaluation (ASE) Programs. (b) Eligible Schools may receive up to $40,000 each to purchase autism-specific tools, including: Other educational resources for children with ASD.

chunks.title: Wancito Francius for State Representative District 108
chunks.text: (c) Schools must submit a detailed DOE application including: Proof of operation for at least two years. (a) The Department of Children and Families (DCF) shall allocate $5,000,000 to support RBTs specializing in behavioral health for children aged 0–13. Training and certification costs for new RBTs. Professional development for existing RBTs. Salary supplements to encourage retention and attract qualified professionals. (c) Priority funding goes to RBTs serving underserved or high-need areas. (a) The DOE and DCF shall collaborate to ensure proper fund allocation and use. (b) Both departments shall submit annual reports to the Governor, Senate President, and House Speaker detailing:

chunks.title: Wancito Francius for State Representative District 108
chunks.text: The number of schools and professionals funded. Recommendations for future funding and program enhancements. (b) The Office of Program Policy Analysis and Government Accountability (OPPAGA) shall conduct periodic audits to ensure compliance and effective fund use. chunks.title: Meet Fabián — Fabián Basabe for Florida State House Representative
chunks.text: Meet Fabián — Fabián Basabe for Florida State House Representative A Visionary Leader, Advocate, and Community Champion Fabián Basabe is a devoted family man, entrepreneur, environmental advocate, and passionate supporter of the arts. Born in New York City to an American mother and Ecuadorian father, Basabe was immersed in a myriad of cultures from an early age. He moved to Quito, Ecuador at age six and attended S.E.K. Elementary School, embracing Latin American traditions before relocating to Miami Beach in 1987.

chunks.title: Meet Fabián — Fabián Basabe for Florida State House Representative
chunks.text: In Miami Beach, Basabe witnessed firsthand the city’s transformation into a global destination as his family restored the historic Boulevard and Breakwater Hotels on Ocean Drive. His early experiences working in the family businesses gave him a deep appreciation for Miami Beach’s diversity and growth. After graduating from Cheshire Academy in Connecticut, Basabe pursued International Relations at Pepperdine University in Malibu, California, where his interest in television media and writing grew. Following college, he was a correspondent on E! Entertainment’s “Young, Rich and Famous” and “Filthy Rich Cattle Drive”, TLC’s “Simple Life to Social Life”, and even had a guest appearance on Oprah.

chunks.title: Meet Fabián — Fabián Basabe for Florida State House Representative
chunks.text: In 2007, Basabe and his wife, Martina Borgomanero, made Miami Beach their permanent home, raising their son Brando and deepening their commitment to the community. Basabe’s philanthropic efforts have supported the Make-A-Wish Foundation, Operation Smile, Spirituality for Kids, and the IBLA Foundation. He has also written for LA Confidential, Paper Magazine and Gotham, among others. In 2022, Basabe was elected to the Florida State House of Representatives for District 106—a district long considered one of the state’s most challenging.

chunks.title: Meet Fabián — Fabián Basabe for Florida State House Representative
chunks.text: Through his unwavering dedication, he has become a champion for the people, building bipartisan coalitions, restoring record funding to his district and earning the respect of many leaders across the aisle. Basabe’s legislative priorities focus on standing firm for educators, law enforcement, and first responders while carrying the struggles of the most vulnerable in his heart. A true friend to the environment, he continues to advocate for environmental preservation and sustainable growth.

chunks.title: Meet Fabián — Fabián Basabe for Florida State House Representative
chunks.text: Reelected for a second term in 2024 with broad support, Basabe exemplifies integrity, honesty, and character in public service, while his leadership reflects a tireless fight for the values that unite communities and a commitment to improving the quality of life for all Floridians. Fabián Basabe’s journey—from entrepreneur and cultural advocate to respected Legislator—demonstrates his unyielding passion for serving the people of District 106 and beyond.

chunks.title: Fabián Basabe for Florida State House Representative
chunks.text: Fabián Basabe for Florida State House Representative As your elected representative, I am proud to serve as a dedicated family man and a long-standing resident of this incredible district. Together, we have achieved tremendous milestones, navigating two primaries and two general elections to solidify our seat at the state’s table in Tallahassee. Our district is now a cornerstone of Florida’s supermajority, ensuring that our voices are heard and our priorities addressed.

chunks.title: Fabián Basabe for Florida State House Representative
chunks.text: When I first ran for office, I was determined to challenge partisanship and bring people together. Today, I remain committed to uniting our community around shared goals to achieve real progress. As a key member of the majority party, I have successfully worked to pass critical legislation and secure funding to meet the needs of District 106. We are revitalizing small businesses, advocating for homeowners and taxpayers, enhancing public safety, modernizing our infrastructure, protecting our beaches and ensuring dignity and care for our elderly. These efforts are only the beginning and I will continue to fight for solutions to improve the quality of life for every resident.

chunks.title: Fabián Basabe for Florida State House Representative
chunks.text: Our challenges are significant, but so are our opportunities. By working together with common sense and determination, we will continue to revitalize and secure our district for generations to come. I am honored to represent you and invite you will join in as we build on our success and strive for even greater achievements. Let’s keep this momentum going—together. “Florida State Fraternal Order of Police believes in the character and moral fiber of Fabian Basabe. We were so impressed with this young man's fervor in wanting to make his district flourish again that we unanimously voted to endorse his candidacy for State Representative in district 106”.

chunks.title: luciabaezgeller.com
chunks.text: The daughter of a Cuban father and Colombian mother, Lucia grew up witnessing the courage and sacrifice that define the American Dream. Her father fled communism in Cuba in the 1980s, surviving a month with almost no food or water while seeking refuge at the Peruvian Embassy before finally reaching the United States. Lucia was raised by her single mother, who worked multiple jobs to ensure her daughter had every opportunity to succeed. Lucia became the first in her family to attend college — an experience that shaped her lifelong commitment to education and standing up for equal opportunity for every resident of District 106.

chunks.title: luciabaezgeller.com
chunks.text: From 2005 to 2020, Lucia taught English and Language Arts at Miami Beach Senior High, where she connected with and inspired thousands of students. Her leadership in education earned her the National Education Association’s Political Advocate of the Year Award in 2013, and she has worked with numerous organizations dedicated to expanding educational opportunity, including the Educational Excellence School Advisory Council, the Association of Latino Administrators and Superintendents, the Hispanic Scholarship Fund, and the League of Women Voters.

chunks.title: luciabaezgeller.com
chunks.text: Lucia earned her undergraduate degree from Spring Hill College and later received both a Master’s in English Education and an Education Specialist degree in Curriculum and Instruction from Florida International University. In 2020, Lucia was elected to the Miami-Dade County School Board, where she continued fighting to strengthen public schools, keep students safe, and ensure every child can succeed. She lives in Miami Beach with her husband, David Geller, and their young daughter. Lucia is also an active volunteer feeding the homeless, advocating for lower costs for families, protecting access to affordable healthcare and bringing civility to our community.

chunks.title: About Commissioner Vicki L. Lopez
chunks.text: Home > Government > Board of County Commissioners > District 5 > About Commissioner Vicki L. Lopez The Honorable Vicki L. Lopez was appointed to the Miami-Dade Board of County Commissioners and sworn in on November 19, 2025, to represent District 5, bringing decades of public service, community leadership, and professional experience to her role. Commissioner Lopez is a graduate of the University of Notre Dame, where she earned a Bachelor of Business Administration in Accounting.

chunks.title: About Commissioner Vicki L. Lopez
chunks.text: Commissioner Lopez has an extensive record of service at both the state and local levels. She was elected to the Florida House of Representatives in 2022 and has since been reelected, advocating for policies that strengthen communities and improve quality of life. Earlier in her career, she served on the Lee County Commission from 1990 to 1993, gaining firsthand experience in local government and constituent services.

chunks.title: About Commissioner Vicki L. Lopez
chunks.text: Her statewide leadership includes appointments by multiple Florida governors to key boards and task forces. These include serving as Chairman of the Governor’s Ex-Offender Task Force, Vice Chair of the Department of Corrections Reentry Advisory Council, and Chairman and Treasurer of the Prison Rehabilitative Industries and Diversified Enterprises Board. She has also contributed to juvenile justice reform as a member of the Florida Senate Juvenile Justice Education Work Group and played a role in shaping tourism policy through the Florida Tourism Commission’s Industry/Government Affairs Committee.

chunks.title: About Commissioner Vicki L. Lopez
chunks.text: A practicing Catholic, Commissioner Lopez is deeply committed to civic engagement, personal well-being, and service to others. Outside of her public service, she enjoys cooking and entertaining, horseback riding, meditation, music, reading, travel, water sports, yoga, walking, and most importantly, spending time with family. With a strong foundation in public service and a deep commitment to her community, Commissioner Lopez serves the residents of Miami-Dade County with experience, integrity, and dedication. 1700 Convention Center Drive, 1st Floor, Contact Us | About the Commissioner Request Public Records

From historic neighborhoods to sweeping bay, river, and ocean views, the eclectic mix of District 5 embodies the best Miami-Dade has to offer residents and visitors alike. This vibrant district includes the cities of Miami and Miami Beach, including the urban neighborhoods of Brickell and Downtown; the working, industrial Miami River; tree-lined Coral Way neighborhoods like The Roads, Silver Bluff and Shenandoah; the South and Mid parts of Miami Beach; and Little Havana and West Flagler, the colorful center of Hispanic culture.

chunks.text: A proud native of Miami-Dade County, Katrina's journey began in the classroom. chunks.title:

chunks.text: Driven by a passion to serve beyond the classroom, Katrina answered the call to public office, serving as a Councilwoman for the City of Miami Gardens. Throughout her tenure, she became a trusted advocate for residents, championing initiatives that promoted education, neighborhood engagement, youth development, and community empowerment. She earned a reputation as a collaborative leader who believed that lasting progress is achieved by bringing people together.

chunks.title:

chunks.text: Her influence extends well beyond elected office. Katrina has become one of South Florida's most respected community leaders, lending her leadership to organizations, civic initiatives, educational programs, and events that celebrate culture, history, and unity. Most notably, she served as one of the principal architects behind the Miami Gardens Juneteenth Experience, helping lead six consecutive years of one of South Florida's premier celebrations of freedom, heritage, and Black excellence. Under her leadership, the event grew into a powerful platform that educates, inspires, and unites thousands of attendees each year.

chunks.title:

chunks.text: Throughout every chapter of her career, Katrina has remained committed to mentoring emerging leaders, encouraging civic engagement, and investing in the next generation. Her unwavering dedication has earned her numerous recognitions, including the 2026 Legacy In Black Gala Visionary Award , honoring her decades of service, transformational leadership, and lasting impact on the people of South Florida.

chunks.title: Linda Cothiere Aristide — Miami-Dade School Board District 1 Runoff, Nov 3 · Punch #92
chunks.text: Linda Cothiere Aristide was born in Cap-Haïtien, Haiti, and came to Miami as a child. Like so many District 1 families, she started out in a public school before she had the language — and came up through it anyway: she grew up in Carol City and graduated from Miami Carol City Senior High. A proud product of Miami-Dade public schools, she earned her associate degree at Miami Dade College and her bachelor's in education at St. Thomas University, then gave her career back to the community that raised her — building adult-education programs that move our neighbors into real careers.

chunks.title: Linda Cothiere Aristide — Miami-Dade School Board District 1 Runoff, Nov 3 · Punch #92

And for the past five years she has talked with South Florida every week, co-hosting The Reyni Talk Show on 1360 AM. At home, education is the family business: her husband, Wallace Aristide, served Miami-Dade schools for more than 30 years — over a decade of them as principal of Miami Northwestern Senior High. ✓ An immigrant herself — educated in the District 1 public schools. ✓ 30+ years of public-school experience in the family she's part of. ✓ A classroom teacher who has been inside our schools — never watching from outside.

chunks.text: Florida ranks last in the nation for teacher pay, and we lose ours to the next county. Direct local dollars to competitive pay and real retention — the smartest investment we can make. Audit district-mandated paperwork and cut duplicative reporting so teachers teach, not document. Protect classroom autonomy and professional judgment within state standards.

chunks.text: Seat working District 1 teachers on the advisory committees that shape curriculum and scheduling. Miami-Dade County School Board, District 1 — general election, Tuesday, November 3, 2026 The two Florida school board District 1 candidates on the Miami-Dade ballot are Linda Cothiere Aristide and Katrina Wilson . They were the top two finishers among seven candidates in the August 18, 2026 primary, and they now face each other in the general election on Tuesday, November 3, 2026 .

chunks.title: Florida School Board District 1 Candidates (Miami-Dade): Linda Cothiere Aristide vs. Katrina Wilson — Nov 3, 2026 Runoff
chunks.text: School board races in Florida are nonpartisan, so every registered voter in District 1 gets a vote in November — whether or not you voted in August. Miami-Dade School Board District 1 was a nonpartisan special election with seven candidates on the ballot. No candidate reached a majority, so under Florida Statute 105.051(1)(b), the top two advance to a runoff at the November 3, 2026 general election: Katrina Wilson (1st) and Linda Cothiere Aristide (2nd). The other five candidates, listed in the table below, were eliminated and are not on the November ballot. Miami-Dade School Board District 1, August 18, 2026 primary — official canvassed results.

chunks.text: The Miami-Dade County School Board is the elected body that governs Miami-Dade County Public Schools. Its members adopt the district budget, set district policy, and hire and evaluate the superintendent. The board approves major contracts, sets attendance boundaries, and decides whether schools open, consolidate, or close. Board members do not manage day-to-day school operations; that responsibility belongs to school administrators and the superintendent. Voter registration deadline: Monday, October 5, 2026. chunks.title: Gloria Romero Roses | Join the Movement for Miami
chunks.text: Gloria Romero Roses | Join the Movement for Miami Rooted in Miami, driven by service, and committed to building a safer, healthier, more affordable future for all. Gloria Romero Roses is a lifelong problem solver, entrepreneur, and community builder running to move Miami forward. She believes we do this by ensuring every Miamian can pursue their freedom to be safe, healthy and prosperous.

chunks.title: Gloria Romero Roses | Join the Movement for Miami
chunks.text: Born in Bogotá, Colombia and raised in South Florida, Gloria grew up watching her single mother, a nurse, work tirelessly to provide a better life. Those experiences shaped her belief that every person deserves a fair shot and a level playing field. She approaches every challenge with data, fairness, and a commitment to real-world results.

chunks.title: Gloria Romero Roses | Join the Movement for Miami
chunks.text: After putting herself through Florida International University while working full-time, Gloria earned her MBA and built a distinguished career in real estate, affordable housing, and community development. She has turned around struggling condominium and homeowner’s associations, led major development projects, and helped revitalize neighborhoods across South Florida. As the owner and operator of an assisted living facility, she worked to ensure residents could live with dignity and safety even when it meant taking personal financial loss. Today, as a small business owner and civic leader, Gloria continues to champion affordability, fairness, and opportunity for all.

chunks.title: Gloria Romero Roses | Join the Movement for Miami
chunks.text: She has served on the boards of the Univision Foundation, genCLEO Action, the Women’s Fund of Miami-Dade, and she is a longtime advocate for the Alzheimer’s Association, representing Florida families in Tallahassee and Washington, D.C. She has worked and understands issues from all sides, from homeowners, to seniors, small businesses and developers, and non-profit leaders.

chunks.title: Gloria Romero Roses | Join the Movement for Miami
chunks.text: A woman of faith, a proud Miamian, and a problem solver, she leads by listening, building consensus, and acting with integrity. She is running to level the playing field for everyday Miamians- to accelerate affordable housing development, expand childcare, and help families and small businesses thrive again. She has built a 40-year career based on solving problems and is ready to hit-the-ground-running on these problems now because every Miamian deserves the freedom to be safe, healthy, and prosperous. Together, we can move Miami forward — ¡Pa’lante!

chunks.title: Gloria Romero Roses | Join the Movement for Miami
chunks.text: Gloria will accelerate construction for affordable housing by expanding access to capital and repurposing underused properties. Also by fixing the way our state government understands what its job is: to accelerate funding for projects and to support how local governments can cut the red tape to get more built, faster. She supports transit-oriented development that connects people to jobs, reduces household costs, and builds thriving mixed-income communities. Affordable Healthcare Access & Alzheimer’s Awareness

chunks.title: Gloria Romero Roses | Join the Movement for Miami

We need practical reforms, not political theater.

chunks.title: On the Issues - Ashley V. Gantt for State Senate
chunks.text: As a former public school teacher in Miami-Dade, Ashley has experienced firsthand the importance of investing in our schools. Equity starts with providing the space and resources to underserved youth to develop the skills they need in order to compete in our changing economy. Our students need unique resources to meet their specific needs to prepare them for successful and full lives, where test preparation isn’t emphasized more than intellectual development.

chunks.title: On the Issues - Ashley V. Gantt for State Senate
chunks.text: Florida needs a fair funding formula to ensure inner-city school districts are receiving equitable funding for resources like books and programing for the creative and performing arts, increased wages for Florida teachers to attract new talent and reduce the student-to-teacher ratio in public schools, and a guarantee that all schools are ADA compliant and provide fair and equal opportunities to students with disabilities.

chunks.title: On the Issues - Ashley V. Gantt for State Senate
chunks.text: Miami-Dade’s housing affordability crisis is in dire need for solutions. Our county’s State of Emergency is due to families’ inability to stay in their homes and find safe housing. As housing costs skyrocket while wages remain stagnant, it’s imperative that we provide affordable housing opportunities to the residents of Florida. By increasing the accessibility of housing vouchers, repairing and improving existing public housing, taxing house flipping and other speculative real estate practices, and instating affordable housing requirements for new real estate development projects we can level the playing field for those who are simply trying to live.

chunks.title: On the Issues - Ashley V. Gantt for State Senate
chunks.text: Miami-Dade County is ground-zero for climate change. Addressing sea level rise for our coastal communities, and providing clean air and water to Floridians should be a top priority in the State Senate. Legal and financial consequences must be levied against polluters, holding them accountable for the destruction of our beaches, water supply, and air. We have a small window of opportunity to enact changes to protect our environment to make sure it flourishes for generations to come.

chunks.title: On the Issues - Ashley V. Gantt for State Senate
chunks.text: As a former public defender, Ashley Gantt has seen the unequitable effects of a broken criminal justice system and we must work towards establishing more restorative justice programs, increased mental health services, and alternatives to incarceration for our youth. Florida is better when we work together to establish programs to reduce recidivism and support the reintegration of returning citizens to our communities.

chunks.title: On the Issues - Ashley V. Gantt for State Senate
chunks.text: Effective and reliable transportation is the cornerstone of a region’s economic health. Investing in eco-friendly public transportation will help create green jobs, improve accessibility for residents in densely populated urban areas, and expand workforce opportunities regionally. Supporting Small Business & Job Creation

chunks.title: On the Issues - Ashley V. Gantt for State Senate
chunks.text: Small businesses are the backbone of our community’s economic sustainability and growth. As State Senator, Ashley will work to ensure equitable pathways to support and opportunities so that small businesses can thrive and grow. Good paying jobs are in dire need to ensure Floridians can afford the rising costs of living, and by attracting employers to our community, we can do just that.

chunks.title: Meet Ashley Gantt - Ashley V. Gantt for State Senate
chunks.text: Meet Ashley Gantt - Ashley V. Gantt for State Senate Ashley Gantt is an attorney, educator, and public servant running to represent Miami-Dade in the State Senate. From the classroom to the courtroom, Ashley has dedicated her career to serving her community. She hopes to bring her experiences to Tallahassee to advocate for the residents of her district.

chunks.title: Meet Ashley Gantt - Ashley V. Gantt for State Senate
chunks.text: Ashley V. Gantt, Esq. is the founder and managing partner of Gantt Legacy Law, P.A. In 2007 Ashley graduated from the University of Florida with a Bachelor of Arts degree in English and became a Teach for America Mississippi Delta Corps (TFA) member. She dedicated two years to national community service, with a mission to close the achievement gap in the Greater Delta region. Ashley returned home to teach in Miami-Dade County Public Schools for seven years before beginning law school.

chunks.title: Meet Ashley Gantt - Ashley V. Gantt for State Senate
chunks.text: In 2016, Ashley graduated from NSU Shepard Broad College of Law. While in law school, Ms. Gantt served as chapter Secretary and President of the Black Law Students Association. She is a member of Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, Inc. and the University of Florida Association of Black Alumni South Florida chapter. Upon her admission to the Florida Bar, Ashley became a Broward County Assistant Public Defender, serving the citizens of Broward County for over two years. She received recognition for her work, earning two consecutive “Hat Trick” Awards from the Broward Association of Criminal Defense Attorneys for attaining not guilty verdicts in at least three successive trials.

chunks.title: Meet Ashley Gantt - Ashley V. Gantt for State Senate
chunks.text: In 2021, Ashley pivoted from working at a large firm to opening her law firm, Gantt Legacy Law, P.A. She specializes in Criminal Defense, Estate Planning and Probate, and Personal Injury. Various life experiences influenced her areas of specialization and continue to fuel her ambition and drive as a practitioner.

chunks.title: Meet Ashley Gantt - Ashley V. Gantt for State Senate
chunks.text: Ms. Gantt continues to be active in her community, serving on the executive board of the T.J. Reddick Bar Association as corresponding secretary, recording secretary, President-Elect and President in the 2020-2021 fiscal year. Ashley is a board member for the Gwen S. Cherry Black Women Lawyers Association and a Florida Bar Wm. Reece Smith Jr. Leadership Academy Fellow. Ms. Gantt also served as the District 2 Trust member on the Citizens’ Independent Transportation Trust in Miami-Dade County. Lastly, Ms. Gantt is an adjunct professor at Nova Southeastern University College of Law.

For District 34. “Understanding our history is essential to building our future.” Elizabeth Jeanty is a resident of Florida Senate District 34, an entrepreneur, community leader, media personality, historian, and candidate for the Florida State Senate. With more than 20 years of experience in nonprofit leadership, business development, and civic engagement, she has dedicated her career to empowering communities through education, advocacy, and service.

chunks.title: Meet Elizabeth | Elizabeth Jeanty for Florida State Senate District 34
chunks.text: A Miami-Dade County resident for over 27 years, Elizabeth was born in the Dominican Republic to Haitian parents. A background that has given her a lived understanding of the Haitian, Latina, and Black communities that make up much of District 34. Fluent in English, Spanish, Haitian Creole, and French, she has built her life's work around bridging cultures, preserving history, and creating opportunity for the many communities she calls her own, and has become a trusted voice across South Florida's diverse neighborhoods.

chunks.title: Meet Elizabeth | Elizabeth Jeanty for Florida State Senate District 34
chunks.text: Elizabeth is the Executive Director and Chairwoman of the Haitian American Historical Society (HAHS), where she leads initiatives dedicated to preserving and promoting the contributions of Haitians to American history. Under her leadership, HAHS has educated thousands about the legacy of the Chasseurs-Volontaires de Saint-Domingue — the more than 550 freemen of color who fought alongside American forces during the Revolutionary War — whose sacrifices are commemorated through the annual Haitian Monument events in Savannah, Georgia.

chunks.title: Meet Elizabeth | Elizabeth Jeanty for Florida State Senate District 34
chunks.text: She is also the host of The Power of Women Show on WLQY 1320 AM in Miami, where she educates and engages the community on issues related to history, civic participation, economic opportunity, leadership, and community empowerment. As the founder of Eliza Consulting Agency LLC and a licensed Florida real estate professional, she has helped individuals, families, and entrepreneurs across every background navigate business, housing, and financial opportunities, always advocating for economic mobility and self-sufficiency.

chunks.title: Meet Elizabeth | Elizabeth Jeanty for Florida State Senate District 34
chunks.text: As a candidate for the Florida State Senate, District 34, Elizabeth's platform is centered on housing affordability, insurance costs, infrastructure and flood resilience, and responsible local governance. She believes leadership is not simply holding a title; it is showing up, listening, educating, and delivering meaningful results for every resident she serves.

chunks.title: Meet Elizabeth | Elizabeth Jeanty for Florida State Senate District 34
chunks.text: Elizabeth's story reflects the full identity of the community she seeks to represent. She carries the shared experience of Haitian, Latina, and Black families across the district. The same challenges of building wealth, owning a home, and securing a future for the next generation. She believes that preserving history and expanding opportunity is not the work of one community alone, but a shared responsibility that unites every family calling this district home. Her leadership is rooted in that shared struggle and shared possibility, building bridges rather than drawing lines, and delivering results for all. Expanding access to affordable homes and protecting homeowners across District 34.

chunks.title: Meet Elizabeth | Elizabeth Jeanty for Florida State Senate District 34
chunks.text: Fighting for relief and fairness for families struggling with rising insurance premiums. Investing in strong infrastructure and flood protection to keep our communities safe and resilient. Promoting transparency, accountability, and leadership that puts residents first. Service is not about a title. It’s about showing up, listening, educating, and delivering results that change lives.

chunks.title: Elizabeth Jeanty for Florida Senate District 34
chunks.text: Elizabeth Jeanty for Florida Senate District 34 Elizabeth Jeanty is running for Florida State Senate to make our communities safer, more affordable, and full of opportunity. Every student deserves the resources to succeed and a bright future. Healthcare is a right, not a privilege. I will fight to make it accessible for all. Florida's foremost advocate for the public education system, low-cost childcare, and parental choice. A voice of moral clarity and moral courage that champions the freedoms that built Miami-Dade. Elect Senator Calatayud in 2026. Líder efectiva, nacida y criada en Miami, que lucha por el futuro de la asequibilidad. La principal defensora de Florida del sistema de educación pública, el cuidado infantil de bajo costo y la elección de los padres. Una voz de claridad y coraje moral que defiende las libertades que construyeron Miami-Dade. Elija a la Senadora Calatayud en 2026.

chunks.title: Alexis Calatayud
chunks.text: Senator Alexis Calatayud is a champion for generational upward mobility, focused on expanding educational and economic opportunities for Miami-Dade residents. Her leadership has led to landmark legislation and significant funding aimed at achieving economic security and self-sufficiency for Floridians. Key initiatives include lowering the cost of living, enhancing community affordability, improving access to affordable housing, children's health insurance, and investing in early childhood education. She also serves on the Jackson Memorial Health System Public Health Trust.

chunks.title: Alexis Calatayud
chunks.text: La Senadora Alexis Calatayud es defensora de la movilidad ascendente generacional, enfocada en ampliar oportunidades educativas y económicas para los residentes de Miami-Dade. Su liderazgo ha resultado en legislación histórica y financiación significativa para lograr la seguridad económica y la autosuficiencia de los floridanos. Sus iniciativas clave incluyen reducir el costo de vida, mejorar la asequibilidad comunitaria, ampliar el acceso a vivienda asequible, seguro médico infantil e invertir en educación temprana. También sirve en el Fideicomiso de Salud Pública del Sistema Jackson Memorial.

chunks.title: Alexis Calatayud
chunks.text: Before being elected to the Florida Senate in 2022, Senator Calatayud dedicated over a decade to advocacy and policy roles in education reform. Currently, as Community Engagement Liaison for the Miami-Dade and Monroe County Early Learning Coalition, she facilitates national learning exchanges. During the COVID-19 pandemic, she served as Chief Lobbyist and Legislative Affairs Director for the Florida Department of Education, advocating for impactful education policies.

chunks.title: Alexis Calatayud
chunks.text: Antes de ser elegida al Senado de Florida en 2022, la Senadora Calatayud dedicó más de una década a roles de defensa y política en reforma educativa. Actualmente, como Enlace de Participación Comunitaria de la Coalición de Aprendizaje Temprano de Miami-Dade y Monroe, facilita intercambios nacionales de aprendizaje. Durante la pandemia de COVID-19, sirvió como Cabildera Principal y Directora de Asuntos Legislativos del Departamento de Educación de Florida.

chunks.title: Alexis Calatayud
chunks.text: A passionate human rights advocate and granddaughter of Cuban political asylum seekers, Senator Calatayud collaborates with nonprofits to support political prisoners and dissidents in exile and promote freedom from authoritarian regimes. She has also trained over 500 university student leaders on higher education affordability issues.

chunks.title: Alexis Calatayud
chunks.text: Defensora apasionada de los derechos humanos y nieta de exiliados políticos cubanos, la Senadora Calatayud colabora con organizaciones sin fines de lucro para apoyar a presos políticos y disidentes en el exilio y promover la libertad de los regímenes autoritarios. También ha capacitado a más de 500 líderes estudiantiles universitarios sobre la asequibilidad de la educación superior. In the Senate, she serves as Chair of the Education Postsecondary Committee and Vice Chair of the Education Pre-K–12 Committee , along with various appropriation committees. With a deep commitment to her role, she is running for election in 2026 to continue serving the constituents of Senate District 38.

chunks.title: Alexis Calatayud
chunks.text: En el Senado, se desempeña como Presidenta del Comité de Educación Postsecundaria y Vicepresidenta del Comité de Educación Pre-K–12 , junto con varios comités de asignaciones. Con un profundo compromiso con su rol, busca la elección en 2026 para seguir sirviendo a los electores del Distrito 38. chunks.text: Message from Senator Alexis Calatayud - Miami’s Community News SAT, OCT 10, 2026 · MIAMI, FL · 90° Miami Community Newspaper Sponsored Content Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... This is your State Senator, Alexis Calatayud. Thank you for the honor of representing your family in Tallahassee for the last four years. As your voice in the State Senate, we are tackling the pressing challenges of reducing cost-of-living and enhancing quality of life, the real issues facing our incredibly diverse community, from Key Biscayne to Homestead.

chunks.title: Message from Senator Alexis Calatayud - Miami’s Community News
chunks.text: There are core American values that we all share, that bind us together. They are just common sense, like an affordable pathway for the middle class to homeownership. I work everyday to fight for our shared values in tangible ways.

chunks.title: Message from Senator Alexis Calatayud - Miami’s Community News
chunks.text: Addressing head-on our homeownership affordability crisis, in 2023 I created Florida’s Hometown Hero down payment assistance program, a NEW pathway for Miamians to purchase their first homes! In the last four years, I fought for $300 million in state investment for our neighbors to make the American Dream of homeownership real through $35,000 at 0% interest downpayment assistance loans to help buy their first home in Miami-Dade, sooner! More than 20,000 families statewide have purchased their first home because of the Hometown Heroes down payment assistance program.

chunks.title: Message from Senator Alexis Calatayud - Miami’s Community News
chunks.text: $50 MILLION IN NEW funding is available for the Hometown Heroes Housing Program on July 13th, 2026. Our program provides as a second mortgage loan up to $35,000 at 0% interest in down payment and closing cost assistance for eligible first-time homebuyers in critical professions – including EARLY LEARNING AND K-12 teachers, nurses, first responders, law enforcement, healthcare workers, and many more. Apply and join the first-time home-owning families in our community living in their new home today because of Hometown Heroes! https://www.floridahousing. org/live-local-act/hometown- heroes-program Connect To Your Customers & Grow Your Business

chunks.title: Richard Lamondin for State Senate
chunks.text: Richard Lamondin is 38 years old. He has a four-year-old son, aging parents he supports, a mortgage in a state where insurance has nearly tripled, and hundreds of employees depending on him every two weeks. He is not running away from those challenges. He is running for office because of them — and because too many families in this district are living the same story without anyone in Tallahassee fighting for them. Right now in Florida, the basics feel impossible. Preschool costs as much as rent. Insurance premiums have nearly tripled. A million people still don’t have health coverage. Our public schools are being systematically defunded.

chunks.title: Richard Lamondin for State Senate
chunks.text: These aren’t accidents. They are the result of thirty years of choices made by people who will never feel them. Richard built a company from the ground up lowering costs for families and businesses across the country. Now he’s running for Florida State Senate because this community deserves a leader with actual skin in the game — and Miami now has a choice. Too many Miami families are one illness or one prescription away from financial disaster. Richard believes health care is a right, not a privilege. And that no one should lose sleep wondering how to pay a hospital bill.

chunks.title: Richard Lamondin for State Senate
chunks.text: In Congress, he’ll work across the aisle to guarantee affordable, high-quality coverage with real choice — protecting the right of anyone who likes their current plan to keep it, while ensuring every family has access to an affordable public option that lowers costs for everyone. He’ll champion legislation to cap out-of-pocket expenses, expand mental-health services, and take on drug companies that keep prices high while posting record profits. Because in the richest country on earth, no one should go bankrupt just to see a doctor or fill a prescription.

chunks.title: Richard Lamondin for State Senate
chunks.text: Every parent knows the cost of child care has become unmanageable — and every study shows that early education changes lives. As a dad of a three-year-old, Richard has seen firsthand how broken and expensive the system is. In Miami, child care often costs as much as rent, and he feels that strain just like so many other families do. His first legislative priority will be to build bipartisan support for affordable, accessible pre-K and child care for every family , raising early-education pay, expanding hours for parents who work nights, and treating early learning like the essential service it is. Because when every child gets a fair start, every family gets a fair shot.

chunks.title: Richard Lamondin for State Senate
chunks.text: Miami has become the most rent-burdened county in the nation, and young people, families, and seniors are being priced out of the communities they built and have called home their whole lives. Richard believes housing isn’t just about real estate, it’s about dignity, stability, and the ability to put down roots and build generational opportunity.

chunks.title: Richard Lamondin for State Senate
chunks.text: In Congress, he’ll work to treat housing as critical infrastructure , just like roads and bridges, so federal dollars flow faster to projects that expand supply and lower costs. He’ll collaborate across the aisle to reduce red tape at HUD, improve the Housing Choice Voucher program, expand first time home buyer tax credits, and restore federal funding for flood-mitigation and resilience projects that protect homeowners and lower insurance costs. Because if our hospitality workers, teachers, and first responders can’t afford to live here, we don’t have a community — we have a crisis.

chunks.title: Richard Lamondin for State Senate
chunks.text: After a lifetime of work, every American deserves peace of mind. The freedom to retire without fear of losing their savings or health care. For every senior in Miami, Social Security and Medicare aren’t handouts — they’re earned promises that must be protected and strengthened. In Congress, Richard will work to preserve and strengthen Social Security, Medicare and Medicaid , ensuring they remain fully funded and off the chopping block. He’ll support measures to protect seniors from skyrocketing prescription-drug prices, safeguard pensions , and expand home- and community-based care so older Americans can age safely and comfortably in their homes.

chunks.title: Richard Lamondin for State Senate
chunks.text: Because the measure of a country isn’t how it treats its wealthiest, it’s how it honors those who’ve worked a lifetime to build it. SD-38 is the number one Democratic state target seat in Florida — and the race that begins to break the corruption that has controlled Tallahassee for far too long. Richard is running against a well-funded incumbent backed by special interests who have kept that majority in place. Your contribution funds the staff, organizing, ads, and the ground operation that wins this seat. Have a question for the campaign? Want to get involved, share your story, or connect with our team?

chunks.title: Richard Lamondin for State Senate
chunks.text: We want to hear from you. Richard is running to be a senator who actually shows up — and that starts now. Reach out and someone from our team will get back to you.

chunks.title: Meet Richard Lamondin — Richard Lamondin for State Senate
chunks.text: Meet Richard Lamondin — Richard Lamondin for State Senate Dad. Husband. Business Owner. First-time Candidate. Richard Lamondin has never worked in government or run for office. But he’s done something Tallahassee insiders haven’t: Built a successful business in Miami from the ground up — creating jobs, helping families and companies lower their utility bills, and giving back to the community he calls home. That’s exactly why we need him in the State Senate.

chunks.title: Meet Richard Lamondin — Richard Lamondin for State Senate
chunks.text: Born and raised in Miami, Richard is the Co-Founder & CEO of ecofi — a company proving that sustainability can be good for both people and business. Under his leadership, ecofi became one of the fastest-growing environmental services companies in the country, earning national recognition for its innovation and impact. Conserved more than 10 billion gallons of water Prevented over 300,000 metric tons of carbon emissions Helped lower utility bills for thousands of renters nationwide

chunks.title: Meet Richard Lamondin — Richard Lamondin for State Senate
chunks.text: But the path wasn’t easy. In the early years, Richard and his brother Lawrence worked multiple jobs while building ecofi from scratch. They didn’t just manage the company — they rolled up their sleeves and did the work themselves, one installation at a time. Today, Richard’s proudest role isn’t CEO. It’s dad to his son Leo, and husband to his wife Martina, right here in Miami. Now he’s stepping up to serve — not as a career politician, but as someone who’s lived the challenges this community faces, and who knows how to get real results. Now, He’s Building a Campaign to Deliver for All of Us.

chunks.title: Meet Richard Lamondin — Richard Lamondin for State Senate
chunks.text: Richard Lamondin isn’t running to be a politician — he’s running because too many politicians have forgotten what real life looks like. From building a clean infrastructure company with his brother to raising a young family right here in Miami, Richard knows what it means to hustle, to worry, to hope. And to show up for others. He built something from the ground up that makes a real impact: Lowering bills, creating jobs, and helping families. Now, he’s bringing that same energy to this campaign. Grandson of a WWII veteran and Teamster. Son of a Canadian immigrant who built his way into real estate. Married to an Italian immigrant and housing nonprofit director.

chunks.title: Meet Richard Lamondin — Richard Lamondin for State Senate
chunks.text: Co-founded ecofi , one of the fastest-growing environmental service companies in the country. Helped save 10+ billion gallons of water and lower bills for thousands of renters. Led by example: In the early years, personally installed water-saving equipment with his brother. Serves on nonprofit boards focused on youth, equity, and mental health: Project Transforming Hope – expanding economic opportunity for underserved youth. Engage Miami – mobilizing young people into civic leadership. ADAPT Foundation – providing mental health and wellness for local youth.

chunks.title: Meet Richard Lamondin — Richard Lamondin for State Senate
chunks.text: Richard is a homeowner, a dad, and a husband who feels the squeeze of high housing costs, rising insurance premiums, and expensive child care — just like the rest of us.

chunks.title: Miami-Dade County – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: Did you know that District 40 encompasses magnificent Miami-Dade? There is no place Ana Maria would rather call home or raise two children with her husband than South Florida. Miami-Dade is a place of opportunity, culture, entrepreneurship, and hardworking families, but too many residents are feeling squeezed by rising costs. Ana Maria’s priority has been, and will continue to be, representing residents and addressing the issues that affect everyday life. That means working to make housing more affordable, cutting taxes and fees where possible, lowering homeowner’s insurance premiums, keeping communities safe, investing in schools, and supporting a strong local economy.

chunks.title: Miami-Dade County – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: As your State Representative and State Senator, Ana Maria has supported record funding for Florida’s public school system, empowered parents to make decisions about their children’s education, and championed more affordable, accessible healthcare. She has fought to keep taxes low, reduce unnecessary regulations on small businesses, and help local employers create good-paying jobs.

chunks.title: Miami-Dade County – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: In Miami-Dade, the affordability crisis is one of the most urgent challenges facing families, seniors, renters, homeowners, and small businesses. Ana Maria is focused on practical solutions that put more money back in residents’ pockets: tax relief, property insurance reform, stronger consumer protections, responsible budgeting, and policies that make it easier to build and preserve affordable and workforce housing. Cut taxes and fees so residents can keep more of what they earn. Support small businesses by reducing unnecessary red tape,  burdensome regulations, and increasing paychecks Strengthen the local economy by helping employers create and retain good-paying jobs.

chunks.title: Miami-Dade County – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: Improve Florida’s unemployment compensation system so it works when residents need it most. Use a responsible, data-driven approach to economic policy that protects both livelihoods and quality of life. Fight to reduce homeowner’s insurance premiums and bring more stability, transparency, and accountability to the property insurance market. Invest in affordable and workforce housing so teachers, nurses, first responders, service workers, young families, and seniors can continue to live in the communities they serve. Support policies that expand homeownership opportunities and protect residents from being priced out of South Florida.

chunks.title: Miami-Dade County – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: Identify short-, medium-, and long-term solutions to address flooding, sea level rise, and community resilience. Protect the integrity of Miami-Dade County’s Urban Development Boundary to preserve the Everglades and safeguard this irreplaceable ecosystem for future generations. Fight unnecessary toll increases that make commuting and daily life more expensive. Protect the neighborhoods, parks, schools, and local institutions that define South Florida’s quality of life. Support law enforcement, first responders, and community-based public safety efforts. Invest in community policing and practical partnerships that build trust between residents and public safety agencies.

chunks.title: Miami-Dade County – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: Support local governments that choose to expand the adoption of body cameras and other accountability tools. Increase access to high-quality, affordable healthcare. Expand telehealth options for seniors, working families, and vulnerable residents. Continue efforts to reduce the cost of prescription drugs.

chunks.title: About Ana Maria – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: A Principled, Independent Voice for South Florida Ana Maria Rodriguez is running for re-election to the Florida State Senate. After serving one term in the Florida House of Representatives from 2018 to 2020, she successfully ran for the Florida Senate, where she has built a strong record focused on improving quality of life for South Florida families, seniors, homeowners, small businesses, and working residents. She was also elected by her peers to serve as Chair of the Miami-Dade Legislative Delegation, a leadership role she continues to hold today.

chunks.title: About Ana Maria – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: Born in Miami to Cuban parents, Ana Maria understands the value of opportunity, hard work, safe communities, and a government that respects the people it serves. Her public service has been guided by a simple priority: help residents keep more of what they earn and make South Florida a more affordable place to live, work, raise a family, and retire. As a state legislator, Ana Maria has worked on issues that directly affect household budgets. She has supported keeping taxes low, reducing unnecessary burdens on small businesses, and strengthening Florida’s economy so employers can create good-paying jobs.

chunks.title: About Ana Maria – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: Ana Maria is especially focused on the affordability crisis facing South Florida. Rising costs are putting pressure on families, seniors, renters, homeowners, and small businesses – she is committed to cutting taxes, opposing unnecessary cost increases, expanding access to affordable and workforce housing, and fighting for real solutions to reduce homeowners’ insurance premiums. As the mother of school-age children, Ana Maria knows that strong schools are essential to strong communities. She has supported record funding for Florida’s public school system, as well as policies that empower parents to make the best decisions for their children’s education.

chunks.title: About Ana Maria – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: She has spent her career advocating on behalf of the people of South Florida, both as a professional and as a public servant. Prior to being elected to the State House, she served on the Doral City Council for eight years and previously worked as the Director of Government and Community Relations for Baptist Health. Currently, she serves as Vice President of the MIAMI Association of REALTORS®, where she advocates for policies that increase homeownership, make housing more affordable, and strengthen community resilience.

chunks.title: About Ana Maria – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: In her spare time, Ana Maria is active in the South Florida community. She has served on the Florida International University President’s Council, as the Honorary Chair of the Autism Speaks Miami Walk, and as a board member for multiple community and philanthropic organizations, including the Coral Gables Community Foundation, the City of Doral Parks & Police 4 Kids advisory board, and the Miami Lighthouse for the Blind organization’s Young Professionals of the Lighthouse Group.

chunks.title: About Ana Maria – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: Ana Maria is a proud Miami native. She attended St. Theresa Catholic School, graduated from Our Lady of Lourdes Academy, earned a B.S. in Communications from Florida International University, and earned an M.S. in Leadership from the Huizenga School of Business at Nova Southeastern University. Her husband, Dr. Clemente Canabal, is a native of Cartagena, Colombia. They live in Miami-Dade County with their two sons, Hermes and Eros.

chunks.title: Miami-Dade Hurricane Preparedness – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: Miami-Dade Hurricane Preparedness – Ana Maria Rodriguez Miami-Dade County stay safe this Hurricane Season by being prepared! Hurricanes can happen quickly, and families may be separated. Create a plan now so everyone knows how to stay safe, communicate, and reunite after the storm. Phone numbers of a pre-assigned contact person for family members to call. List and contact information of family members, friends, neighbors and physicians. A safe place to store important documents in a waterproof container or bag. How you will get assistance if needed for older adults or those with functional needs in the home. How to turn off the water, gas and electricity safely.

chunks.title: Miami-Dade Hurricane Preparedness – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: Prepare an emergency supply kit with essentials your family may need during or after a storm. Keep everything in one safe place and make sure all family members know where to find it. Keep loose items in airtight plastic bags. Gather the kit’s items in easy-to-carry containers or duffel bags. Put them within reach, near the exit you use most often. Check and update your kit at least once a year. Your hurricane supply kit should contain: 7-day supply of water (one gallon per person per day, including pets) Battery-powered portable television or radio with extra batteries

chunks.title: Miami-Dade Hurricane Preparedness – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: Sanitation and hygiene items, such as instant hand sanitizing gel, disinfectant wipes, moist towelettes, toilet paper, and feminine hygiene products Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), such as masks and gloves Kitchen accessories and cooking utensils Extra clothing, blankets and sleeping bags Photocopies of identification, insurance, prescriptions, household inventory, credit cards and your utility bill Copies of important documents such as birth certificates, adoption certificates, marriage licenses, divorce papers, Social Security cards, passport, green cards, will, insurance policies (home, auto, life, health, etc.), bank statements

chunks.title: Miami-Dade Hurricane Preparedness – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: Prescription medications, eyeglasses, contact lens solution and hearing aid Telephone that is not dependent on electricity and/or a cell phone Formula, baby food, diapers and pacifiers Pet carriers, leashes, shot records, and food for each animal evacuating with you As you prepare for a storm, don’t forget to include your pets in your emergency plans. If you stay with family, friends, or neighbors, make sure your pets go with you.

chunks.title: Miami-Dade Hurricane Preparedness – Ana Maria Rodriguez
chunks.text: If you stay home during a storm, keep your family and pets together in a safe area. Use a crate or carrier for your pet, keep their collar and ID tag on, and consider microchipping them in case you become separated. If you live in an evacuation zone, mobile home, or unsafe structure, go to a pet-friendly evacuation center. During emergencies, Animal Services operates pet-friendly evacuation shelters. No pre-registration is needed, and shelter information will be shared as necessary. For everyone’s safety, pets will be evaluated by a licensed veterinarian before admission. chunks.text: Focused on Families, Affordability, and Results . Ana Maria Rodriguez has spent her career advocating for the people of South Florida as a public servant, community leader, and working mother. chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Files Consumer Protection Lawsuit Against Evolve Construction and Its Principals for Preying on Florida Hurricane Vict
chunks.text: TALLAHASSEE, Fla. —Attorney General James Uthmeier filed a lawsuit against Evolve Construction, LLC, Evolve Construction & Restoration, Inc., and six principals and officers, alleging the companies and individuals used unfair, deceptive, and unconscionable practices to prey on Florida consumers who needed residential roof repair, roof replacement, and water and mold remediation after Hurricanes Ian and Milton.

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Files Consumer Protection Lawsuit Against Evolve Construction and Its Principals for Preying on Florida Hurricane Vict
chunks.text: “These companies knocked on doors after the storms, promised fast repairs, took insurance money, and left Florida families with unfinished homes and liens on their property,” said Attorney General James Uthmeier . “More than 60 percent of the consumers who complained to our office are seniors. The fraudsters should expect to be held accountable.”

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Files Consumer Protection Lawsuit Against Evolve Construction and Its Principals for Preying on Florida Hurricane Vict
chunks.text: “Our investigations and administrative prosecutions resulted in 12 final orders against Ahmed Darkawi, the loss of his license, and an opportunity for affected homeowners to help recover funds they lost,” said Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation Secretary Melanie S. Griffin . “We will continue working with Attorney General Uthmeier and our partners to pursue every action available under Florida law to prevent future victims, protect consumers, and safeguard the integrity of Florida’s construction industry.”

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Files Consumer Protection Lawsuit Against Evolve Construction and Its Principals for Preying on Florida Hurricane Vict
chunks.text: “Everybody has heard of storm chasers, but most homeowners have not heard of storm scammers,” said William Webb, Chairman of the Florida Home Builder’s Association . “These are the type of people that come in right after the storm claiming to be a contractor to help you out whether it’s your roof or other items that need attention. These scammers are out to take advantage of our uninformed homeowners that are already under duress from the storm. Don’t become a victim.”

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Files Consumer Protection Lawsuit Against Evolve Construction and Its Principals for Preying on Florida Hurricane Vict
chunks.text: The complaint, filed in the Twentieth Judicial Circuit in Lee County, alleges that the corporate defendants and the individual defendants operated as a common enterprise. At least 80 consumers from Lee, Charlotte, Sarasota, Hillsborough, Polk, Osceola, Manatee, Volusia, St. Lucie, St. Johns, and Broward Counties have filed complaints with the Attorney General’s Office. More than 60 percent of those consumers are seniors. Consumers alleged paying more than $1 million for work they did not receive as promised.

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Files Consumer Protection Lawsuit Against Evolve Construction and Its Principals for Preying on Florida Hurricane Vict
chunks.text: Many insurance payments ranged from $5,000 to $80,000 per property, and the complaint alleges the defendants often collected those funds in full while leaving work unfinished or never started.

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Files Consumer Protection Lawsuit Against Evolve Construction and Its Principals for Preying on Florida Hurricane Vict
chunks.text: According to the complaint, the defendants solicited homeowners in their homes immediately after the storms, misrepresenting the quality and scope of the work and how quickly repairs would begin and be completed. Sales representatives who were not licensed contractors offered “free” roof inspections and held themselves out as “experts.” The complaint alleges those representatives never held the home-solicitation sale permits required by Florida law. They promised expedited permits, accelerated timelines, and the best possible insurance settlement—then, the State alleges, took consumers’ insurance benefits and failed to perform the work.

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Files Consumer Protection Lawsuit Against Evolve Construction and Its Principals for Preying on Florida Hurricane Vict
chunks.text: The complaint further alleges that defendants required consumers to sign an unconscionable “Contingency Agreement” that failed to provide a good-faith itemized estimate of costs, omitted cancellation language required by Florida law, imposed an unlawful cancellation penalty recharacterized as “liquidated damages,” and functioned as an unlawful assignment of insurance benefits. When consumers tried to cancel or obtain refunds for work that was never performed, the defendants allegedly refused. Some consumers received only partial or poor-quality work that failed inspections and caused additional property damage.

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Files Consumer Protection Lawsuit Against Evolve Construction and Its Principals for Preying on Florida Hurricane Vict
chunks.text: The complaint alleges the defendants threatened to place liens on homes—and in some cases recorded liens, including for inaccurate amounts, and pursued foreclosure—even when no work was performed and no materials were purchased. Defendants also sent representatives to consumers’ homes to collect payments, leaving some consumers feeling physically threatened. The corporate defendants are Evolve Construction, LLC, a Florida limited liability company organized in 2021 with its principal place of business in Naples, and Evolve Construction & Restoration, Inc., a Florida corporation formed in 2023, also based in Naples. The individual defendants named in the complaint are:

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Files Consumer Protection Lawsuit Against Evolve Construction and Its Principals for Preying on Florida Hurricane Vict
chunks.text: Patrick Antoine  of Lee County, Florida, an authorized member of Evolve Construction, LLC and secretary of Evolve Construction & Restoration, Inc.; Ahmed Darkawi  of Hennepin County, Minnesota, an original registered agent, authorized person, and former manager of Evolve Construction, LLC; Jarret Gross  of Martin County, Florida, an authorized member of Evolve Construction, LLC; Aleksandr Guldshtadt , also known as Alex Gold, of Los Angeles County, California, former CEO of Evolve Construction & Restoration, Inc. and a former authorized member, registered agent, and manager of Evolve Construction, LLC; John Vincent  of Los Angeles County, California, manager of Evolve Construction, LLC; and

chunks.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier Files Consumer Protection Lawsuit Against Evolve Construction and Its Principals for Preying on Florida Hurricane Vict
chunks.text: Jaser “Jay” Zaabri  of Los Angeles County, California, a manager of Evolve Construction, LLC and chief financial officer of Evolve Construction & Restoration, Inc. The lawsuit brings two counts under the Florida Deceptive and Unfair Trade Practices Act: one against the corporate defendants for unfair, deceptive, or unconscionable practices in the marketing, sale, and provision of residential construction and restoration services, and one against the individual defendants for their direct participation in, knowledge of, and ability to control those practices.

chunks.text: ICYMI: Attorney General James Uthmeier Activates Price Gouging Hotline as Hurricane Isaias Approaches | My Florida Legal ICYMI: Attorney General James Uthmeier Activates Price Gouging Hotline as Hurricane Isaias Approaches TALLAHASSEE, Fla.— Attorney General James Uthmeier activated Florida's Price Gouging Hotline as Hurricane Isaias heads toward the Florida Panhandle. Isaias became a major hurricane Friday morning and is expected to make landfall tonight or early Saturday.

chunks.title: ICYMI: Attorney General James Uthmeier Activates Price Gouging Hotline as Hurricane Isaias Approaches | My Florida Legal
chunks.text: "Protecting Floridians isn't a seasonal job, and this hotline ensures that there is a simple process to report unconscionable increases in prices," said Attorney General James Uthmeier . "Whether it's a storm, a scam, or a greedy corporation, our office will enforce the law." Under Florida's price gouging statute, section 501.160, Florida Statutes, it is unlawful during a declared state of emergency to charge unconscionable prices for essential commodities and services needed to prepare for or recover from the storm. These include food, water, ice, gasoline, lumber, equipment and hotel rooms.

chunks.title: ICYMI: Attorney General James Uthmeier Activates Price Gouging Hotline as Hurricane Isaias Approaches | My Florida Legal
chunks.text: The law applies within the counties covered by Governor DeSantis's state of emergency : Baker, Bay, Calhoun, Citrus, Columbia, Dixie, Escambia, Franklin, Gadsden, Gilchrist, Gulf, Hamilton, Holmes, Jackson, Jefferson, Lafayette, Leon, Levy, Liberty, Madison, Okaloosa, Santa Rosa, Suwannee, Taylor, Wakulla, Walton and Washington. Violators face civil penalties of $1,000 per violation, up to $25,000 for multiple violations committed in a single 24-hour period. Criminal sanctions may also apply. Floridians who suspect price gouging can report it through MyFloridaLegal.com or by calling 1-866-9-NO-SCAM. For more information on price gouging, click here .

chunks.title: About the CFO
chunks.text: Blaise Ingoglia serves the citizens of the state of Florida as the state's Chief Financial Officer, State Fire Marshal, and member of the Florida Cabinet. Meet your Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia Blaise Ingoglia built his reputation by holding government accountable, long before he held public office. Originally from New York, Blaise moved to Spring Hill, Florida, in 1996 with just $1,600 to his name. He soon found success as a mortgage broker and later founded Hartland Homes, a homebuilding company dedicated to helping working families achieve the dream of homeownership.

chunks.title: About the CFO
chunks.text: Ingoglia’s interest in public service was sparked in 2007 when he noticed local governments “going wild” spending property tax dollars. That frustration led him to launch Government Gone Wild , a viral video series and public seminar campaign aimed at exposing government waste and out-of-control spending. His YouTube channel has garnered nearly 8 million views, helping to spark a broader national conversation about fiscal responsibility.

chunks.title: About the CFO
chunks.text: Over time, Blaise became a respected voice for transparency and common-sense governance, serving in the Florida Senate, representing the 11th district, from 2022 to 2025, and the Florida House of Representatives from 2014 to 2022 in the 35th district, as well as chairman of the Republican Party of Florida from 2015 to 2019. But long before that, he was just a homebuilder with a camcorder, a YouTube channel, and a determination to make sure taxpayer dollars were treated with respect. And yes, fittingly for someone named Blaise , he now serves as Florida’s State Fire Marshal and works every day to support firefighters in their life-saving missions.

chunks.title: About the CFO
chunks.text: CFO Blaise Ingoglia’s top priority is making Florida more affordable, with a focus on lowering property taxes and reducing insurance costs for hardworking families. Chief Financial Officer of the State of Florida Blaise Ingoglia serves as Florida’s Chief Financial Officer and State Fire Marshal, overseeing billions of dollars in taxpayer assets and leading the Florida Department of Financial Services. His role includes managing the state’s finances, rooting out fraud, increasing financial transparency, and supporting first responders across the state.

chunks.title: About the CFO
chunks.text: As CFO, Blaise continues his mission to protect taxpayers by shining a light on government inefficiency and promoting smart budgeting practices. He also oversees Florida’s Division of Unclaimed Property, helping reunite residents with lost funds, and leads the Criminal Investigations Division, which fights insurance fraud, arson, and public assistance abuse. Whether working to improve financial literacy, strengthen emergency response systems, or increase efficiency in state spending, CFO Ingoglia brings the same passion, energy, and no-nonsense attitude that first put him on the map.

chunks.title: About the CFO
chunks.text: Blaise lives in Spring Hill with his wife, Julie, and their dogs. He is a proud husband, father, entrepreneur, and public servant who believes that good government starts with accountability and a lot of common sense. The state's CFO also serves as Florida's State Fire Marshal. The Division of State Fire Marshal provides various fire-related training, education and services throughout the state, from assisting local fire departments by conducting consumer education to training citizens at one of the finest fire-training colleges in the state.

chunks.title: About the CFO
chunks.text: Florida's CFO serves as one of three constitutionally elected state executives of the Florida Cabinet, which comprises the Chief Financial Officer, the Attorney General, and the Commissioner of Agriculture and Consumer Services. Governor Ron DeSantis and the Florida Cabinet serve as a board of directors, or agency heads, governing such matters as the purchase of state lands; clemency matters; state bond, trust and fund management; veterans' affairs; state law enforcement administration; tax collection; power plant and transmission line sitings; and financial and insurance regulation for the state of Florida.
